Following the supplied citation, the root पै॒ ends in -ai and has no ओ-anubandha. Before the non-śit suffix क्तवतुँ, the final ऐ becomes आ (आदेच उपदेशेऽशिति), so the root becomes पा.

The suffix क्तवतुँ loses its anubandhas and becomes -तवत्. Because the root is not ओदित्, the ending stays -तवत् and does not change to -नवत् (no नत्व).

The result is पा + तवत् = पातवत्. The uninflected stem is given.

<answer>पातवत्</answer>

The root is ष्वष्क् (ṣvaṣk), "to go", with the final anunāsika vowel as an anubandha. The anudātta mark on that vowel makes the root ātmanepadī.

1. The initial ष् becomes स् by "धात्वादेः षः सः", giving स्वष्क्.
2. The anudātta mark falls on the anubandha, not on the root's own vowel. So the root's vowel is udātta and "एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्" does not block the augment. The root takes इट्.
3. Adding तुमुँन् (the मु and न् are dropped as anubandhas, leaving तुम्) with इट् gives स्वष्कितुम्.

<answer>स्वष्कितुम्</answer>

पुर् (तुदादि, अग्रगमने) कुटादि वर्ग में आता है, ऐसा मेरी स्मृति से है, पुष्ट नहीं किया। इसलिए "कुटादिभ्योऽणिन्ङित्" से ल्युट् ङित्वत् होता है और गुण नहीं होता। ल्युट् के "यु" को "अन" आदेश होता है, और "रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे" से न का ण होता है। इस प्रकार पुर् + अन = पुरण बनता है।

पुरँ के ँ को इदित् (नुम्-आगम) मानने पर रूप अलग (पुन्रण) होता, पर मैंने इसे नहीं माना।

<answer>पुरण</answer>

I read the root as मिध् (the final ऋ is an anubandha marker, so the root is not इदित् and takes no नुम्). It is not on the list of aniṭ roots, so it takes the connecting vowel इट्. The suffix तृच् becomes तृ. The सार्वधातुक/आर्धधातुक rule for guṇa of the इ vowel applies before the suffix, giving मेध्. The result is मेध् + इ + तृ, which yields the agent-noun stem मेधितृ.

<answer>मेधितृ</answer>

The root is अन्स् (Curadi, "समाघाते"). The Curadi class takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, which gives अन्सि. Adding the agent suffix ण्वुँल्, where वु becomes अक, gives अन्सि + अक. The णिच् is then elided, leaving अन्स् + अक. The upadhā (penultimate sound) of the root is न्, not short अ, so no vṛddhi applies. Finally, न् before the jhal sound स् becomes anusvara (नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि), giving the stem अंसक.

<answer>अंसक</answer>

In the Dhatupatha form एठँ॒, the nasal ँ is the anubandha. The root is एठ्, and its anudātta accent marks it as anit, so क्त (त) takes no इट्.

1. एठ् + त: after an aspirated stop (झष्), त becomes ध by झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः, giving एठ् + ध.
2. ष्टुत्व turns ध into ढ, giving एठ् + ढ.
3. झलां जश् झशि turns ठ् into ड्, giving एड् + ढ.
4. ढो ढे लोपः drops the first ड्, giving एढ. The preceding vowel ए is not अण्, so it is not lengthened.

<answer>एढ</answer>

The root is वृह् (ū-anubandha, so iṭ is optional by 7.2.44), and the suffix is तुमुँन्, which becomes तुम्.

1. The ṛ takes guṇa before तुम्, giving वर्ह्.
2. With the optional iṭ, this gives वर्हितुम्.
3. Without iṭ, it would give वर्ढुम् instead.

Both forms are valid, so I give one.

<answer>वर्हितुम्</answer>

The root is अबिँ (idit), so the nasal is inserted and it becomes अम्ब्. Adding the suffix अनीयर् (अनीय) gives अम्बनीय. The root vowel is short अ, so no guṇa applies.

<answer>अम्बनीय</answer>

The root is चञ्चु (चन्चुँ), "to go", with the final उँ as an anubandha, so the stem is चञ्च्. The suffix अनीयर् leaves अनीय after dropping its anubandha र्.

- The root is seṭ by default, and the suffix begins with a vowel, so no iṭ-prohibition applies and the stem takes the linking vowel: चञ्च् + अनीय.
- The penultimate nasal gives no guṇa. Before च् the nasal is written ञ् by homorganic assimilation.

This gives चञ्चनीय. The citation spells the nasal as न्, so चन्चनीय would be the same form in that spelling.

<answer>चञ्चनीय</answer>

I applied the following steps to the root षै (class 1, "to waste away").

1. The initial ष् becomes स्, giving सै.
2. The suffix ण्वुँल् reduces to वु, which is replaced by अक.
3. The final ऐ of the root becomes आ (ādeśa upadeśe 'śiti), giving सा.
4. Before a ṇit kṛt suffix, the root-final आ takes the augment य् (ātो yuk), as in गै → गायक.

This gives सा + य् + अक = सायक.

<answer>सायक</answer>

Ignoring the accent, the ँ in तृक्षँ is the anunāsika marker. In this notation it marks an anudātta root, so the root is anudātta and ekāc (one vowel). By the rule ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt (7.2.10), such a root does not take the connecting इ before क्त. I am relying on my reading of the ँ as an anudātta marker, which I could not check against the source.

1. The suffix क्त becomes त and is kit, so there is no guṇa of ऋ.
2. तृक्ष् + त has क्ष् followed by त. Since क्ष् is क् + ष्, the क् drops by skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca (8.2.29), leaving तृष् + त.
3. The त after ष् becomes ट by ṣṭutva, giving तृष्ट. The parallel is तक्ष् → तष्ट.

<answer>तृष्ट</answer>

Under the traditional analysis, शवँ is the root शव्, with the anunasika vowel as an it-marker, and it is a single-syllable root. I assumed it takes the connecting vowel इ before क्तवतु, because I could not confirm that it is aniṭ. I also took the शूनवत् type, which belongs to श्वि, as not applying here. This gives शव् + इ + तवत् = शवितवत्, the uninflected stem. I am not fully certain of the इट् treatment.

<answer>शवितवत्</answer>

I derived this by hand and did not check it against the Dhatupatha text.

The root पष is in the Curadi class, so it takes the suffix णिच् (-aya-). The णिच् causes vṛddhi of the penultimate short a, giving पाष-. The verb stem is therefore पाषयति. Adding शतृँ (-at) in the present active gives the participle stem पाषयत्.

<answer>पाषयत्</answer>

The root रगिँ (class 1, "to go") carries the इत् vowel इँ, so it is an इदित् root and takes the nasal insertion नुम्, giving रङ्ग्. Because the root is इदित्, the nasal is not dropped before the क्-marked suffix (the elision rule अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति applies only to non-इदित् roots). The suffix क्त reduces to त, and the root takes the connecting vowel इट्, so रङ्ग् + इ + त gives रङ्गित.

<answer>रङ्गित</answer>

I treated the root as इदित् (the marker इँ), so it takes the नुम् nasal insertion, giving निन्ज्. I took it as अनिट् because of the anudātta marker (णिजिँ॒), so क्तवतु is added without इट्. Because the root is इदित्, the nasal is not dropped before the कित् suffix (6.4.24 applies only to roots without इदित्). The final ज् becomes क् before the त of the suffix (कुत्व), and the nasal assimilates to ङ् before क्. This gives निङ्क्तवत्.

I am least sure of the class and the nasal. The related root णिजिँर् is normally class 3, and I did not confirm that this citation sits in class 2, so the nasal rests on the supplied marker इँ.

<answer>निङ्क्तवत्</answer>

Because the root चटँ carries the इत् marker ँ, it is इदित् and takes the नुम् augment (इदितो नुम् धातोः, 7.1.58), giving चण्ट्. Being Curadi, it takes the suffix णिच्. Before क्त the connecting vowel इट् is added and the णिच् is dropped (णिलोप). This gives चण्ट् + इ + त = चण्टित.

<answer>चण्टित</answer>

The root is यौट् (the ऋ is only an anubandha), and adding तृच् gives the agent-noun stem यौटितृ. I formed this from my recollection of the root's shape and did not check the Dhatupatha entry.

1. The suffix तृच् loses its anubandha and leaves the ending तृ.
2. The root's vowel औ is already a vṛddhi vowel, so no guṇa or vṛddhi change applies.
3. I assumed the suffix takes the connecting vowel इ, since the root is not among the aniṭ roots I know of. That gives यौट् + इ + तृ = यौटितृ.

<answer>यौटितृ</answer>

I formed this from the root अव् (अवँ), "to protect, move, desire…", with the past participle suffix क्त (त).

1. The suffix क्त is a कित् suffix that begins with a झल् consonant (त).
2. Under सूत्र 6.4.20, ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवामुपधायाश्च, the व् of अव् and its preceding vowel अ are replaced by ऊठ् (ऊ) before such a suffix.
3. This gives ऊ + त, so the participle stem is ऊत (nominative ऊतः).

I am not fully certain whether the root's ँ marker would allow an alternative form with the connecting vowel इ (अवित). I chose ऊत because it is the form I recall as attested.

<answer>ऊत</answer>

I read the root as विध् with the final अँ as an anubandha. The root has one vowel and an anudātta accent, so it takes no connecting इ (aniṭ). This accent-based aniṭ reading is my assumption, not something I confirmed against a source. If the root were seṭ, the form would instead be विधितवत्.

1. Adding क्तवतु (suffix त-वत्) to विध् gives विध् + तवत्.
2. The ध् of the root changes to द् before the following त, giving विद्ध + त.
3. The त then becomes ध, giving विद्ध + वत्.
4. The stem is therefore विद्धवत्.

<answer>विद्धवत्</answer>

Forming the stem from the root भष् (class 1, "to threaten or revile"):

1. The suffix ल्युँट् leaves अन after the markers are dropped, since ल् and ट् are dropped and यु is replaced by अन.
2. The root vowel is a short अ, so no guṇa or vṛddhi applies.
3. This gives भष् + अन. The rule रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे changes न to ण after ष, so the result is भषण.

<answer>भषण</answer>

Since the verb is in class 10 (Curādi), it takes the suffix णिच्. The root's vowel gets guṇa, so क्षिप् becomes क्षेपि. The agent suffix तृच् then gives क्षेपयितृ, with the connecting इ and the णिच् stem forming -अय-.

<answer>क्षेपयितृ</answer>

The root णिलँ becomes निल् because the initial ण् changes to न (णो नः). The suffix ण्यत् becomes -य, and ṇit does not block guna. The short medial इ takes guna to ए, as in लिह् → लेह्य. This gives नेल्य.

<answer>नेल्य</answer>

The root तुबिँ has the इँ anubandha, which marks it as इदित्, so a nasal is inserted (इदितो नुम् धातोः) and the root becomes तुम्ब्. The suffix ल्युँट् loses its anubandhas to leave यु, which is replaced by अन (युवोरनाकौ). Adding this to तुम्ब् gives तुम्बन, the stem of the neuter noun तुम्बनम्.

<answer>तुम्बन</answer>

This is the verb कॄ (विक्षेपे, class 6) with the agent suffix तृच्, which leaves the ending तृ.

- कॄ is a seṭ root, so the ārdhadhātuka suffix takes the augment इट्, giving कॄ + इ + तृ.
- तृच् is not कित् or ङित्, so the rule ऋत इद्धातोः (which gives कीर्ण in the participle) does not apply. Instead the root vowel takes गुण: ॠ → अर्, giving कर्.
- The result is कर् + इ + तृ = करितृ.
- By the rule वृतो वा, the इट् may optionally be lengthened, which would give करीतृ. I give one form.

<answer>करितृ</answer>

The root चितिँ (class 10, "to remember") has an इदित् marker, so it takes नुम्, giving चिन्त्. As a Curadi root it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, which gives चिन्तय्. Adding तृच् with the connecting vowel इ gives चिन्तयितृ.

<answer>चिन्तयितृ</answer>

I formed the past participle (क्त) of the root अक्ष् (ending in ष्) "to pervade". Because the root is ऊदित् (marked with ऊँ), it takes optional इट् under 7.2.44. By 7.2.15 (यस्य विभाषा), क्त then takes no इट् at all, so the suffix attaches directly as त.

- अक्ष् + त gives अक्ष्त.
- After ष्, the त changes to ट by ष्टुत्व, giving अक्ष्ट.
- The initial क् of the conjunct क्ष्ट drops by 8.2.29 (स्कोः संयोगाद्योः), giving अष्ट.

This parallels तक्ष् becoming तष्ट. I reasoned the derivation from the rules and recalled अष्ट as an attested form but did not check it against a source.

<answer>अष्ट</answer>

The root is युज् (class 10, संयमने). Class 10 roots take the suffix णिच्, and this gives the causative-type stem योजि-.

The suffix क्तवतु् begins with a consonant, so इट् is inserted before it. Because इट् applies, the णि is not elided, and the formation is योजि + इ + तवत् = योजितवत्. The anubandhas of क्तवतु् drop away, leaving the stem तवत्.

<answer>योजितवत्</answer>

Applying तुमुँन् to the root मज् (class 1, "to sound") with the connecting vowel इ gives मजितुम्. I took the root to be सेट् (taking इट्) by default, since I could not confirm from the citation whether it is अनिट्. That is an assumption, so treat the result with that caveat.

<answer>मजितुम्</answer>

The root is अह् (with the anunāsika marker removed), and the suffix ल्युँट् leaves यु after its markers are dropped. यु is replaced by अन (युवोरनाकौ, Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.1.1), so the stem is अह + अन. The root's vowel is short अ, so no guṇa or vṛddhi applies, and no retroflexion (ṇatva) is triggered. The resulting neuter stem is अहन.

<answer>अहन</answer>

I formed this by applying ण्यत् (ṇyat) to the root दृ. The root ends in ऋ, and ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (3.1.124) assigns ṇyat to such roots. The ण् marker triggers vṛddhi of the final ऋ, which gives दार् (दृ → दार्). Adding य then gives दार्य.

<answer>दार्य</answer>

The root is वटिँ, where the इँ is an anubandha (इदित्), so a nasal is inserted and the root becomes वण्ट्. As a Curadi root it takes the suffix णिच्, giving वण्टि. Before the suffix यत्, which is an अनिट् ārdhadhātuka, the णिच् is dropped by "णेरनिटि". The result is वण्ट्य.

<answer>वण्ट्य</answer>

The root चुट्ट् (cuṭṭ, "to become small") is Curadi, so it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving चुट्टि. The vowel उ is followed by a conjunct, so it is heavy and takes no guṇa. In the present, शप् becomes अय. शानच् then becomes आन with the मुक् augment, so आन turns into मान after the अ-final stem. This gives चुट्टय + मान → चुट्टयमान.

<answer>चुट्टयमान</answer>

The root is ध्रस् (उँध्रसँ, "उञ्छे", class 9). Its initial उँ is an it-marker, so it is dropped. The final सँ is anudātta, so the root is aniṭ and ktavatu takes no इ. I am relying on memory of the Dhatupatha and Pāṇinian rules for the anudātta marking, not on a checked source. The optional iṭ rule for udit roots (उदितो वा, 7.2.56) applies only to ktvā, so it does not apply here.

The suffix क्तवतुँ reduces to वत् once its it-markers are removed. Joining it to the bare root gives ध्रस् + तवत् = ध्रस्तवत्.

<answer>ध्रस्तवत्</answer>

I treat छ्यु as ending in ु with an anudātta marker, so it is aniṭ and takes no इट् before तुमुँन्. The final न् of तुमुँन् is dropped as an anubandha, leaving the suffix तुम्. Since तुम् is ārdhadhātuka, the root's final उ takes guṇa (उ → ओ), giving छ्यो + तुम्. I did not check the root against a Dhatupatha text, so the aniṭ status rests on the accent marker in the supplied citation.

<answer>छ्योतुम्</answer>

This is a derivation from the root खोर्, where the ऋँ in the citation is an anubandha marker and is dropped. Since the root ends in a consonant, the suffix ण्यत् is added by the rule ऋहलोर्ण्यत्, leaving the suffix as -य. The ण् would normally trigger vṛddhi, but the root's penultimate vowel is ओ, which is not अ, so it stays unchanged. This gives खोर् + य = खोर्य.

<answer>खोर्य</answer>

Applying the steps as I understand them:

1. बस्तँ is a Curadi root meaning "to injure", so it takes the suffix णिच् (चुरादिभ्यो णिच्). This gives बस्ति, with no vrddhi of the medial अ, as in कथयति and गणयति.
2. The agent suffix ण्वुँल् reduces to वु, which is replaced by अक (युवोरनाकौ). Before it the णिच् is elided (णेरनिटि), giving बस्त् + अक.
3. The result is the stem बस्तक, which parallels कथक and गणक.

<answer>बस्तक</answer>

The root is अजिँ (class 10), whose anubandha इँ marks it as इदित्. By इदितो नुम् धातोः it takes the नुम् augment, giving अञ्ज्. The class 10 suffix णिच् then gives the causative-type stem अञ्जि. Adding the agent suffix तृच् with the connecting इट् gives अञ्जयितृ.

<answer>अञ्जयितृ</answer>

This is a derivation from the standard rules, and I did not check the Dhatupatha entry itself. The root is कित् (class 3, "to know"), and I take the Lat participle with शतृँ.

1. Class 3 roots reduplicate. The velar of the reduplicating syllable becomes palatal (कु-ह-चु), so कित् becomes चिकित्.
2. The class-3 विकरण शप् is elided by श्लु (luk). The शतृँ suffix leaves the ending -अत्.
3. The root is reduplicated (अभ्यस्त), so नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुः blocks the नुम् augment. This gives चिकितत् and not चिकिन्तत्.

<answer>चिकितत्</answer>

This is the root स्रम्भ् (written स्रन्भुँ in this citation), whose final उँ is an anubandha. The root carries the anudātta accent, so it takes no इट् before क्तवतु. Because क्तवतु is कित्, the medial nasal drops (6.4.37), giving स्रभ् + तवत्. The final भ् then becomes ब् and the following त becomes ध (झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः), giving स्रब्धवत्. The related form विश्रब्ध is formed the same way.

<answer>स्रब्धवत्</answer>

I read the root as माह्, with the final ऋँ as a marker (anubandha) that is dropped, and the suffix तव्यत् as तव्य.

The citation form माहृँ॑ carries a svarita mark on the marker, which makes the root ubhayapadī. The root vowel is unmarked, so it is udātta, which makes the root seṭ (it takes the connecting इट्). I am inferring this accent convention rather than confirming it against a Dhatupatha source.

The derivation is then माह् + तव्य → माह् + इ + तव्य → माहितव्य. If the root were instead aniṭ, the form would be माढव्य.

<answer>माहितव्य</answer>

The root रच् (class 10, Curadi) takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving the stem रचि-. The suffix क्तवतु् (past active participle) is then added with the connecting vowel इ. This yields रचितवतु, whose uninflected stem ends in त्: रचितवत्.

<answer>रचितवत्</answer>

The form is जटित. This assumes the ँ on जटँ is only a notation marker and does not make the root anudātta and therefore aniṭ, which would give जट्ट instead. I could not confirm that from the table, so I relied on जटित being the form actually used in Sanskrit (as in रत्नजटित). On that basis, जट् (class 1, "सङ्घाते") takes the connecting इ before the क्त suffix (त), giving जट् + इ + त = जटित.

<answer>जटित</answer>

Here is the derivation, assuming the root is aniṭ (not checked against a source):

- The root ष्टिघ् loses its initial ष् by the rule that replaces initial ष् with स्. The ट् of ष्टि also reverts to त्, giving स्तिघ्.
- The root is a single syllable with an anudātta vowel, so I took it as aniṭ. The suffix तुमुँन् therefore reduces to तुम् with no इट् augment.
- The ārdhadhātuka suffix triggers guṇa of the root vowel, giving स्तेघ्.
- After the aspirate घ्, the त् of the suffix becomes ध्, and the घ् then becomes ग्. This gives स्तेग्धुम्.

<answer>स्तेग्धुम्</answer>

I derived this by hand and did not check it against a reference. The root अञ्चुँ (written अन्चुँ, "to move; to worship") takes the past active participle suffix क्तवतुँ, which becomes -वत्. The suffix is preceded by the connecting इ, giving अञ्च् + इ + वत्.

Two forms are possible. By 6.4.24, the root's nasal is dropped before क्त-type suffixes, giving अचितवत् in the sense of "moving". By 6.4.30 (नाञ्चेः पूजायाम्), the nasal is kept in the sense of "worship", giving अञ्चितवत्. The given meaning includes both senses, so both are valid. I chose the first, the nasal-dropped form for the first-listed sense of movement, because the instruction asks for exactly one form.

<answer>अचितवत्</answer>

Here सीकृँ॒ is the root सीक्, with ऋ as the anubandha. It means "to sprinkle". The long ई in the root's penultimate position blocks guṇa. The root is seṭ, so the suffix तृच् (the चित् marker drops, leaving तृ) takes the connecting vowel इ. This gives सीक् + इ + तृ = सीकितृ.

<answer>सीकितृ</answer>

I read the root as ग्लुह् (the ऊँ is only an anubandha, ऊदित्). For the class 1 present active participle, the steps are:

1. Class 1 inserts शप् (अ) between the root and the suffix.
2. The suffix शतृँ leaves अत्.
3. शप् is pit, so it is not ṅidvat. The short penultimate उ of the root therefore takes guṇa (7.3.86), giving ग्लोह्.
4. The stem is ग्लोह् + अ + अत् = ग्लोहत्.

I did not apply the special lengthening ऊ of 6.4.89, which is stated for the root गुह्. I assumed it does not extend to ग्लुह्, so that step is the main uncertainty.

<answer>ग्लोहत्</answer>

The root तर्दँ (तर्द्, "to kill") has a nasalised final vowel as its anubandha. I read this as the ordinary उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत् marker on an अ, not as an इदित् marker, so it takes no नुम् augment and the root stays तर्द्.

The suffix ल्युँट् leaves यु after the markers drop, and यु becomes अन by यु-वोरनाकौ. The root has no change before it, so the form is तर्द् + अन = तर्दन, given as the stem.

<answer>तर्दन</answer>

The root is षस्तिँ (षस्त् with the इँ marker), so the steps are:

1. The root is इदित्, so नुम् is inserted after its vowel (इदितो नुम् धातोः). This gives षनस्त्.
2. The initial ष् becomes स् (धात्वादेः षः सः), giving सनस्त्.
3. The न् becomes anusvara before the following स् (नश्च), giving संस्त्.
4. The root ends in a consonant, so ण्यत् applies (ऋहलोर्ण्यत्). The ण् and त् drop as markers and the suffix is -य.
5. There is no vṛddhi, because the penultimate letter of the stem is स्, not अ.

The result is संस्त्य. I worked this out from memory of the rules and did not check it against a text.

<answer>संस्त्य</answer>

The root दण्ड (class 10, "to punish") takes the Curadi suffix णिच्, giving the stem दण्डय-. The agent suffix तृच् is added with the connecting इ, giving दण्डयितृ. The question asks for the uninflected stem, so I give दण्डयितृ rather than the nominative दण्डयिता.

<answer>दण्डयितृ</answer>

I formed this by hand rather than from a reference.

The root कृष् has an anudātta vowel (कृ॒), so by the rule एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात् it takes no इट् before the suffix. The suffix तव्यत् becomes तव्य after dropping its markers. It is a non-कित् ārdhadhātuka suffix, so the root vowel takes guṇa: कृ → कर्. The ष् then changes the dental त् to ट्, giving कर्ष्टव्य.

Some grammatical traditions also allow क्रष्टव्य for this root. I have given only the guṇa form.

<answer>कर्ष्टव्य</answer>

Tentative derivation: the root is खुर् (to cut), with the nasal marker on the vowel dropping out. I could not confirm from memory that it belongs to the कुटादि group of Tudadi roots. I assumed it does. Roots in that group behave as ङित् before non-ञित्/णित् suffixes, which blocks guṇa of the उ, so the form is खुर् + इ + तव्य. If the root is not in that group, the form would instead be खोरितव्य.

<answer>खुरितव्य</answer>

Here is the derivation:

1. The root चुटिँ (cuṭi, class 10, "to cut") carries the anubandha इँ, so it takes the nasal augment (इदित् insertion). The nasal assimilates to ट, giving चुण्ट्.
2. As a Curādi verb it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving चुण्टि-.
3. The agent suffix तृच् is added with the connecting इट्, and णिच् becomes -अय-, giving चुण्टयितृ.

<answer>चुण्टयितृ</answer>

I formed this from the root as given, स्फर्, taking the suffix ण्यत् as -य with the ण् and त् markers dropped. Because the suffix carries the ण् marker, the penultimate short अ of the root takes vṛddhi (अत उपधायाः), so स्फर् becomes स्फार्. Adding -य gives the stem स्फार्य.

<answer>स्फार्य</answer>

I treated the root as दृफ् (ṛ-vowel, final फ्), taking the ँ as a marker only. फ is not among the roots that take no इट् (the traditional list of such roots), so the root is सेट् and takes इ before the suffix. The suffix क्तवतुँ reduces to तवत्, which gives दृफ् + इ + तवत्. The uninflected stem is therefore दृफितवत्. This rests on my recollection of that list, which I did not check against a source.

<answer>दृफितवत्</answer>

This follows the standard rules, but I have not checked the form against a source text.

छदिँ is an इदित् root, so it takes a nasal infix and becomes छन्द्. In class 10 it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving छन्दि-. The suffix क्तवतुँ becomes तवत्, and it takes the augment इट्, so the णिच् is retained. The result is छन्दितवत्.

The upadha of छन्द् is न्, not अ, so there is no vṛddhi.

<answer>छन्दितवत्</answer>

The root is कील् (class 1, "to bind"), which takes the connecting vowel इ before the infinitive suffix तुमुँन् (तुम्). The form is therefore कील् + इ + तुम् = कीलितुम्. I treated the root as set (इट् taking) from memory of its conjugation (कीलति, कीलिता), not from a rule I checked here. The guṇa substitution does not apply, because the long ई is not replaced.

<answer>कीलितुम्</answer>

The verb is धूञ् (class 9, "to shake"). Rule 7.2.44 makes the इट् augment optional before a valādi suffix, so two stems are valid: धवितृ (with इट् and guṇa) and धोतृ (without). I chose the form with इट्.

<answer>धवितृ</answer>

This is my best derivation, but I'm not fully certain of the vowel grade.

1. The root पॄ in the Curadi class takes the causative-type suffix णिच्.
2. The final ऋ takes vṛddhi before the ṇit suffix (अचो ञ्णिति, 7.2.115), giving पार्. I am assuming this vṛddhi takes precedence over the ṛ → ur substitution (7.1.102), which would have given पूर्. That precedence is the uncertain step.
3. The णिच् is then dropped before the ārdhadhātuka suffix ल्युँट्, which becomes -अन.
4. The न् becomes ण् after र्, giving the neuter noun stem पारण.

If the ur substitution applies instead, the form would be पूरण.

<answer>पारण</answer>

I formed it from the root सुर् (षुर् becomes सुर् by धात्वादेः षः सः) with the suffix तृच्, whose च् is only an anubandha, leaving तृ.

1. The root is a consonant-final root that takes the इट् augment before this ārdhadhātuka suffix, giving सुर् + इ + तृ.
2. The suffix तृच् is not ङित्, and the class-6 शप्-substitute श does not apply to it, so nothing blocks guṇa.
3. The penultimate short उ is a laghu upadhā, so it takes guṇa (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च) and becomes ओ.
4. The result is सोरितृ.

The kuṭādi rule making ñit and ṇit suffixes ङित् does not affect तृच्, so it does not change this.

<answer>सोरितृ</answer>

This is the root दुहिँर् (class 1, "to torment"), whose इँ marker makes it इदित्, so a नुम् augment is inserted: दुह् → दुन्ह्. The suffix ण्यत् leaves the plain ण्य after dropping ण् and त्. Guṇa and vṛddhi do not apply here, since the penultimate sound is the inserted न् rather than a vowel, and the final ह् is not a vowel. Before the झल् sound ह्, the न् becomes anusvara, giving दुंह्य.

<answer>दुंह्य</answer>

Removing the marker इँ and applying the ण→न substitution for a ṇ-initial root gives the root निन्द् (with the nasal inserted because the marker is इँ), "to blame". The suffix क्त takes the augment इट्, giving the past participle stem निन्दित.

<answer>निन्दित</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, not checked against a Dhatupatha text, and I did not verify the root entry itself.

1. The root भृशिँ has the anubandha इँ, so it takes a nasal insertion (नुम्) and becomes भृंश्.
2. As a class 10 verb, it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving भृंशि (present stem भृंशय-).
3. The suffix क्तवतुँ becomes -तवत् once its markers drop, and इट् is inserted: भृंशितवत्.

The question asks for the uninflected stem, so I give the stem with -तवत् rather than the nominative form with -तवान्.

<answer>भृंशितवत्</answer>

The root ष्वदँ (class 10, "to taste") has initial ष् replaced by स् by the rule धात्वादेः षः सः, giving स्वद्. Class 10 adds the causative-type suffix णिच्, which gives vṛddhi of the vowel (स्वाद्) and the form स्वादि. Then तव्य is added with the connecting vowel इ, giving स्वादयितव्य.

I treated the ँ marker as not triggering nasal insertion here, since I recall the attested forms as svādayati. I'm not fully certain of this.

<answer>स्वादयितव्य</answer>

I treated the root as रम्ब्, because the इ anubandha in रबिँ (a nasal-inserting root) adds a nasal. Adding अनीय gives रम्ब् + अनीय. There is no guṇa, since the root's vowel is not in the penultimate position. Then रेफ followed by न् changes न् to ण् (रषाभ्यां नो णः), because only vowel and labial letters intervene. This yields रम्बणीय.

<answer>रम्बणीय</answer>

I could not settle with certainty whether the ँ marker on वजँ makes the root aniṭ (no connecting इ). I assumed it is set (सेट्) by analogy with the related root व्रज, whose past participle is व्रजित. On that assumption, वज् takes the connecting इ before क्तवतु, giving the stem वजितवत्.

<answer>वजितवत्</answer>

The root is नट् (class 10), so the stem takes the णिच् suffix: नाटि. Here उपधा-वृद्धि lengthens the root vowel, giving नाट् + णिच्. Adding क्त with the connecting इ gives नाटित. I did not settle whether the anunasika marker on नटँ blocks the vṛddhi, so I followed the ordinary Curadi pattern; if the marker does block it, the form would be नटित.

<answer>नाटित</answer>

I treated this as the root ष्मिङ् (स्मि after ष→स) taken in the Curadi class as the table specifies, so the stem takes the णिच् suffix.

1. स्मि + णिच् gives स्माययति by vṛddhi (स्मै) and then अय्.
2. With क्त्वा there is no prefix, so the suffix stays क्त्वा and does not become ल्यप्.
3. क्त्वा takes the इट् augment here, so the णिच् is not dropped. This gives स्मायि + इत्वा, which is स्माययित्वा.

I did not apply the special ātva (स्मापय-) rule for causing fear or wonder, since the meaning here is अनादर.

<answer>स्माययित्वा</answer>

I read the root as षमँ (ṣam) with the initial ष् becoming स्, giving सम्. I took the ँ marker as showing the root is anudātta, so it takes no connecting इ and is treated as aniṭ. The root-final म् before तुम् becomes an anusvāra-nasal, giving सन्तुम्. This rests on my assumption about the marker, and I could not confirm it against the Dhatupatha. If the root were seṭ, the form would instead be समितुम्.

<answer>सन्तुम्</answer>

I formed this from the root गुङ् (गु, "to sound"), adding the agent suffix ण्वुल्.

1. The suffix ण्वुल् becomes अक, because ण् and ल् drop as markers and वु is replaced by अक.
2. The suffix carries the marker ण्, so the root's final उ takes vṛddhi and becomes औ. The ङ् in the root is only an ātmanepada marker and does not block this.
3. औ before the vowel अ becomes आव्, giving गाव् + अक = गावक.

<answer>गावक</answer>

The root भू takes the suffix तव्यत्, whose final त् is an anubandha, so the suffix is effectively तव्य. The final त् marks the suffix as accented on the final syllable, but it does not change the form.

The suffix is a non-ārdhadhātuka (ārdhadhātuka) suffix, so guṇa applies to the root's ū: भू becomes भो. Before the vowel-initial अ in तव्य, the ो becomes अव्, giving भव्. The suffix begins with त, not a vowel, so the suffix is added directly to भो without an intervening इ: भो + तव्य → भो-तव्य. Then the rule एचोऽयवायावः applies, because ो is followed by त, which is a consonant, not a vowel.

Here the suffix begins with त, which is a consonant. That rule only applies before a vowel, so it does not apply here. Instead, the question is whether the root takes the connecting vowel इ. भू is seṭ (it takes इ), so the form is भो + इ + तव्य. Then ो + इ becomes अव् + इ, giving भवितव्य.

The result is भवितव्य, meaning "that which must be, or is to be."

<answer>भवितव्य</answer>

The root षलँ (class 1, "to go") begins with ष, which becomes स by the rule that an initial ष in a root is replaced by स. This gives सल्. I took the anunāsika marker on the vowel to be an accent-related marker that does not change the form. The root is a regular set root, so the suffix क्त्वा, reduced to त्वा, takes the connecting vowel इ. This gives सलित्वा.

<answer>सलित्वा</answer>

Applying the suffix अनीयर् to the root दिव् (दिवुँ, class 4) gives the form below. After the anubandhas are removed, the root is दिव् and the suffix is अनीय. The suffix is ārdhadhātuka, and the root's penultimate short इ is replaced by guna (ए) under the rule for a short penultimate vowel (7.3.86). This gives देव् + अनीय, and the ordinary rule for न् changing to ण् does not apply here.

<answer>देवनीय</answer>

Following the Dhatupatha citation, the root is षस्तिँ ("to sleep", class 2). The steps are:

1. The final इँ is an anubandha, so the root proper is षस्त्.
2. The initial ष् becomes स् by the rule that replaces the initial ष of a root with स (धात्वादेः षः सः). This gives सस्त्.
3. Because the root is इदित् (it carries the इ marker), it takes the nasal augment नुम् after its vowel (इदितो नुम् धातोः), giving सन्स्त्.
4. The suffix अनीयर् is added. The vowel of the suffix is added directly, with no connecting इ, which gives सन्स्त + अनीय = सन्स्तनीय.
5. The न् before the sibilant स् becomes anusvara (नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि), so the final form is संस्तनीय.

<answer>संस्तनीय</answer>

I could not identify this root with confidence, so the answer rests on an assumption. I read the citation as the root माह्, with ऋँ as an anubandha, and took the meaning "to measure".

The root is not among the aniṭ roots ending in ह (दह्, दिह्, दुह्, नह्, मिह्, रुह्, लिह्, वह्). So I treated it as seṭ, and the suffix तृच् takes the augment इट्. That gives माह् + इ + तृ = माहितृ. The long आ is unchanged, and the suffix letters च् is only an anubandha and drops out.

<answer>माहितृ</answer>

This is a best reading of the input, not a certain one. I took the cited root "अद्टँ" to be the Curadi root अट्ट (aṭṭ, "to disrespect"), with the ँ as an anubandha marker.

As a class 10 root it takes the सार्वधातुक-style णिच् (ṇic) suffix, giving अट्टि. The suffix तव्य then follows with the connecting इट्, and guṇa of the इ gives अय. The result is अट्टयितव्य.

<answer>अट्टयितव्य</answer>

The root विष्क (class 10) takes the Curādi suffix णिच्, giving the stem विष्कि. Before the ārdhadhātuka suffix यत्, णिच् is dropped (ṇeraniṭi), which leaves विष्क्य. I did not check whether Pāṇini's rules would instead call for ण्यत् on this consonant-final root. I followed the suffix the table specifies.

<answer>विष्क्य</answer>

This is the root वश् ("to desire", class 2), taking the gerundive suffix तव्य. I am treating the root as aniṭ, so no इ is inserted. I am recalling that from memory of the aniṭ root list, not checking it against a source. The final श् of the root changes to ष्, and the following त becomes ट by assimilation, giving वष्टव्य.

<answer>वष्टव्य</answer>

The root is पुल् (pul), with the final अ of पुलँ being the anubandha. It is a single-syllable root with no special accent marking, so it takes the connecting इ (it is seṭ). The infinitive suffix तुमुँन् reduces to तुम् once its anubandhas are removed. The ārdhadhātuka suffix तुम् is not कित् or ङित्, so the short उ in the penultimate syllable takes guṇa and becomes ओ (पुल् → पोल्). Adding the connecting इ and the suffix gives पोल् + इ + तुम् = पोलितुम्.

<answer>पोलितुम्</answer>

The root is क्रन्द् (the अनुनासिक on the vowel is only an anubandha), taken in class 10 with the णिच् suffix, giving क्रन्दि-. The suffix यत् is added after this णिजन्त stem (by अचो यत्). Before यत्, which has no इट्, the णिच् is dropped (णेरनिटि). There is no vṛddhi, because the penultimate letter of क्रन्द् is न्, not अ. The resulting stem is क्रन्द्य.

<answer>क्रन्द्य</answer>

Reading the citation पिटँ as the root पिट् (the ँ marks the final inherent अ as an anubandha, not an इदित् root, so there is no नुम् insertion), the absolutive is formed as follows:

1. The suffix is क्त्वा, which becomes त्वा after removing the anubandha क्.
2. The root is a set root, so इ is inserted: पिट् + इ + त्वा.
3. क्त्वा is कित्, so the root vowel takes no guṇa.

This gives पिटित्वा.

<answer>पिटित्वा</answer>

The root is तक्ष् (तक्षूँ, "to make thin", class 1). Its ऊँ marker makes the इट् augment optional before endings like क्त. The rule "यस्य विभाषा" (7.2.15) forbids इट् before क्त for roots that have an optional इट्, so the suffix attaches directly.

1. तक्ष् + त: the ष् turns the suffix's त into ट, giving तक्ष्ट.
2. By "स्कोः संयोगाद्योः" (8.2.29), the initial क् of the conjunct क्ष is dropped before the झल् consonant, giving तष्ट.

The past participle stem is तष्ट.

<answer>तष्ट</answer>

In class 10, the root षहँ (meaning "to bear") takes the causal-type suffix णिच्. The initial ष् becomes स्, so the stem is सहि. Before क्त the stem takes the augment इट् (सहि + इ + त). The णिच् is then dropped before क्त when इट् is present (णि-lopa by 6.4.52). This gives सहित.

<answer>सहित</answer>

I formed the agent noun from the root मृष् (मृषँ, class 4, "to endure"), using the suffix तृच्.

1. The root carries the anudātta accent, so it is seṭ. The suffix therefore takes the augment इट्, giving मृष् + इ + तृ.
2. Guṇa applies to the root vowel ऋ, which becomes अर्. This gives मर्ष् + इ + तृ.
3. The result is the uninflected stem मर्षितृ. The inflected nominative singular would be मर्षिता.

I decided the seṭ status from the accent marking alone and did not check it against a grammar text. If the root were treated as aniṭ, the form would instead be मर्ष्टृ.

<answer>मर्षितृ</answer>

This is a derivation from the root वृजिँ with the suffix ल्युँट्.

1. The suffix ल्युँट् becomes ल्यु, and then ल्यु becomes अन by the rule युवोरनाकौ.
2. The root is इदित् (the इ in वृजिँ is an anubandha), so it takes a नुँम् augment, giving वृ-न्-ज्. The न् is placed after the vowel, so the penultimate sound is न्, not the ऋ, and no guṇa applies. This is the same pattern as बृंहण.
3. The न् becomes ञ् before ज्, giving वृञ्ज्, and adding अन gives वृञ्जन.

The result is the neuter stem वृञ्जन.

<answer>वृञ्जन</answer>

The root is जम् (the anubandhas उँ are dropped), meaning "to eat". The suffix क्त reduces to त. The root is seṭ, so इट् is inserted: जम् + इ + त. The rule आदितश्च (7.2.16) does not block this, because the root is not ādit; the उदित marker only affects क्त्वा. The resulting stem is जमित.

<answer>जमित</answer>

Following the standard rules for a class 10 root, I formed this as follows. The root पिल् takes the णिच् suffix (चुरादिभ्यो णिच्), giving पिलि. The short penultimate इ then takes guna before णिच् (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च), giving पेलि. Adding the connecting vowel इट् and तुमुँन् gives पेलयितुम्.

I could not confirm what the anunāsika marker on पिलँ signals, so I treated it as an ordinary anubandha with no effect on the formation.

<answer>पेलयितुम्</answer>

I read the root as ऋत् with the final इ as an anubandha. I did not verify this against the Dhatupatha entry. Adding ण्वुँल्, the ण्वुल् suffix, gives the following:

- The ण्वु of the suffix is replaced by अक (ण्वुल् → अक).
- The root vowel ऋ is a light penultimate vowel, so it takes guṇa (ऋ → अर्) by the rule for light penultimate vowels.
- The result is अर्त् + अक = अर्तक.

If the root were instead ऋतिँ with a nasal-inserting anubandha, the form would be ऋन्तक. I went with the reading that has no nasal insertion.

<answer>अर्तक</answer>

This is a standard formation, though I did not settle what the anunasika marker on मिलँ implies for iṭ or for any special sandhi rule.

1. The root is मिल्, class 6, "to meet".
2. The suffix तुमुँन् leaves the ending -तुम्. The anubandhas ु and न् drop out, and the इट् augment is inserted because the root is seṭ.
3. तुमुँन् is ārdhadhātuka and not ṅit, so the penultimate short इ takes guṇa and becomes ए.
4. The result is मेल् + इ + तुम्, which gives मेलितुम्.

<answer>मेलितुम्</answer>

The root खषँ is marked with a nasal anubandha (ँ), so it is इदित्. By *इदितो नुम् धातोः* (7.1.58) it takes the augment नुम्, giving खन्ष. Before the jhal letter ष, the न् becomes anusvāra (8.3.24), giving खंष.

The suffix तव्यत् loses its anubandha to become तव्य. The root is सेट्, so the augment इट् comes between root and suffix, giving खंष + इ + तव्य. As a gerundive in -a, the stem is खंषितव्य.

<answer>खंषितव्य</answer>

The root उखिँ is इदित् (the इ is an anubandha), so it takes the nasal augment नुम् (7.1.58), giving उन्ख्, where the nasal becomes ङ् before ख, so उङ्ख्. The root is सेट्, so क्त्वा takes the augment इट्. Since क्त्वा after a सेट् root is not कित् (1.2.18), the nasal is not dropped. The result is उङ्ख् + इ + त्वा.

<answer>उङ्खित्वा</answer>

The root is गुर्द्, with the final nasalised अ (the ँ on द) as an anubandha. The accent mark ॒ shows it is ātmanepadī. Because the ँ marks a final vowel, not an इ-it, the root takes no नुम् (7.1.58).

The root is anudāttet, so it is सेट् and takes the इट् augment before तुम्. The उ in the root is a light penultimate vowel, and तुमुन् is ārdhadhātuka, so it takes guṇa (7.3.86): गुर्द् becomes गोर्द्.

This gives गोर्द् + इ + तुम् = गोर्दितुम्.

<answer>गोर्दितुम्</answer>

I formed this by applying vṛddhi to the root's short a before the ṇit suffix ण्यत्. I did not apply the nasal insertion (नुम्) that the idit marker ँ would normally trigger. For this root the ordinary placement of the nasal after the last vowel would give an odd cluster, and I know of no attested nasalized form, but I am not certain of this point.

The steps are:

- The root is पर्प्, with the anubandha ँ removed.
- ण्यत् leaves the suffix -य, and its ण् marker triggers vṛddhi of the penultimate short a, so पर्प् becomes पार्प्.
- Adding the suffix gives पार्प्य.

<answer>पार्प्य</answer>

The root is झॄ, with the ष् as an anubandha, and it takes क्तवतु.

1. Strip the suffix markers: क्तवतुँ gives -तवत्, with the क् and उँ dropped. The suffix is not सेट्, since the root is monosyllabic and ends in ॠ, so there is no इट् and the form is झॄ + तवत्.
2. By ऋत इद्धातोः (7.1.100), the ॠ becomes इर्. By हलि च (8.2.77) the इ is lengthened, giving झीर् + तवत्.
3. By रदाभ्यां निष्ठातो नः पूर्वस्य च दः (8.2.42), the त of the suffix becomes न after the र्. The result is झीर्णवत्, with ण् by the retroflexion of न after र् (8.4.1).

This is the uninflected stem.

<answer>झीर्णवत्</answer>

Here जुतृँ is the root जुत् (class 1, "to shine"). The ऋ is an anubandha, and the accent mark shows the root is ātmanepada. The root vowel उ is not anudātta, so the root is seṭ and takes the augment इट्.

The suffix क्तवतु has an anubandha क्, so it is kit and blocks guṇa. That gives जुत् + इ + तवत् = जुतितवत्.

<answer>जुतितवत्</answer>

The root is पठ् (class 1, "to speak distinctly"). The suffix क्त्वा becomes त्वा, since the anubandha क् is dropped. The root ends in a consonant and the suffix is not अ-initial, so the iṭ augment must be decided. पठ् is seṭ, so इ is inserted: पठ् + इ + त्वा. The suffix is kit, which blocks guṇa, so the result is पठित्वा.

<answer>पठित्वा</answer>

This is a standard application of the ṇvul suffix to the root, with no prefix.

1. The root is तुभ् (class 4, "to harm"). The anubandha ँ is a marker and is dropped, so no nasal is inserted.
2. The suffix ण्वुँल् is reduced to वु by dropping the markers ण् and ल्. Then वु is replaced by अक (युवोरनाकौ, Pāṇini 7.1.1).
3. Because the suffix has the marker ण्, the short penultimate उ of the root takes guṇa and becomes ओ (7.3.86). This gives तोभ् + अक.

<answer>तोभक</answer>

The root मडिँ has the इदित् marker, so it takes nasal insertion (नुम्) and becomes मण्ड्. It ends in a consonant, so ण्यत् applies by ऋहलोर्ण्यत्. The ण् marker triggers vṛddhi of the penultimate अ (अत उपधायाः), giving मण्ड् → माण्ड्. Adding ‑य gives the stem माण्ड्य, "to be adorned".

<answer>माण्ड्य</answer>

The root is षगेँ, where the final एँ is an anubandha, so the bare root is षग्. The initial ष् becomes स् by the rule धात्वादेः षः सः, giving सग्. I take this root to be seṭ, since I know of no rule that blocks इट् here. So क्तवतुँ, reduced to तवत् after dropping its anubandhas, is added with the connecting इ: सग् + इ + तवत् = सगितवत्. The citation form of the stem is सगितवत्.

<answer>सगितवत्</answer>

This is a derivation from the dhātu स्मि (the initial ष् becomes स्, by the rule that replaces ṣ with s at the start of a root). It is formed with the causative-type suffix णिच्, as Curādi roots are, and then the agent suffix ण्वुल्.

1. स्मि + णिच् → स्मै + इ → स्मायि. Because णिच् carries the marker ण्, the final vowel takes vṛddhi.
2. ण्वुल् → अक, with the ending of the stem dropped: स्माय् + अक.

The result is स्मायक.

<answer>स्मायक</answer>

Formation: the root is बृहिँ (bṛhi, class 1, "to grow; to sound"). The anubandha इँ marks it as idit. By the rule *idito num dhātoḥ* (7.1.58) it takes the nasal augment नुँम्, giving बृंह् (bṛṃh).

The suffix ण्वुँल् loses its markers. The ण् and ल् drop, and the वु is replaced by अक (*yuvor anākau*, 7.1.1). This gives the agent noun stem बृंहक.

Neither guṇa nor vṛddhi applies to the root vowel:
- The ṇit vṛddhi rules (7.2.115–116) do not reach ऋ, because the root does not end in a vowel and its penultimate letter is not अ.
- Guṇa (7.3.86) needs a light penultimate vowel. After the nasal augment, the penultimate sound is the nasal, not ऋ.

This matches बृंहण and बृंहित, which also show no guṇa.

<answer>बृंहक</answer>

Here the root is गडिँ (gaḍi), and the इँ is an anubandha that marks the root as इदित्. An इदित् root takes the नुम् augment, which gives the base गण्ड् (gaṇḍ). The root is anudāttet (ātmanepadī) and therefore seṭ, so the suffix तव्य is added with the connecting vowel इ. This gives गण्ड् + इ + तव्य = गण्डितव्य.

<answer>गण्डितव्य</answer>

This is a rough derivation from memory, not a checked reference.

1. The anubandha इँ in पचिँ marks the root as इदित्, so it takes the nasal augment (नुम्) and becomes पञ्च्.
2. As a class 10 root, it takes the suffix णिच्, giving पञ्चि.
3. The suffix अनीयर् is an ārdhadhātuka suffix with no इट् augment (aniṭ). Before such a suffix, णिच् is dropped (णेरनिटि).
4. This gives पञ्च् + अनीय = पञ्चनीय. The न does not become ण because nothing in the word triggers retroflexion.

<answer>पञ्चनीय</answer>

जृभिँ (जृम्भ्) में इदित् होने से नुम् का आगम होता है, इसलिए धातु का रूप जृम्भ् बनता है। क्त (त) से पहले इट् का आगम होता है, इसलिए जृम्भ् + इ + त से जृम्भित बनता है।

<answer>जृम्भित</answer>

I formed this from the root snas (ष्णसुँ). In the Dhatupatha the initial ष्ण becomes स्न, and the final उँ is a dropped anubandha. Adding तृच् gives the agent noun, and since the root is udit, the iṭ augment is optional (7.2.44). I chose the form with iṭ and did not verify it against a Dhatupatha or Kaumudi text, so the root's iṭ status rests on my recollection of that rule. The other valid form is स्नस्तृ.

<answer>स्नसितृ</answer>

The root is पुष् (Divadi, with the इ-anubandha-free stem पुष्), and the suffix ल्युँट् becomes -यु, which is replaced by -अन (by युवोरनाकौ). ल्युट् is not ङित् or कित्, so the root's उ takes guṇa and becomes ओ. The ण-substitution (ṇatva) then applies after ष्, giving पोषण.

<answer>पोषण</answer>

Taking the root as खुज् (the anubandha उँ marks it as उदित्), the absolutive with क्त्वा can be formed in more than one way. Under the rule उदितो वा (7.2.56), क्त्वा takes the इट् augment optionally. This gives खुजित्वा with इट्, or खुक्त्वा without it (ज् becomes क् by चोः कुः).

With इट्, the rule रलो व्युपधाद्धलादेः संश्च (1.2.26) makes क्त्वा optionally kit. That would allow खोजित्वा as well. I give the form where क्त्वा is kit and no guṇa applies.

<answer>खुजित्वा</answer>

I formed this by attaching क्तवतुँ to मुट् with the connecting vowel इ, which I assumed because I could not recall a rule making मुट् an अनिट् root. The suffix reduces to तवत्. Since क्तवतुँ is कित्, there is no guṇa of the root vowel. This gives मुटितवत्.

<answer>मुटितवत्</answer>

The root रेपृँ has a final ऋ that is an anubandha (indicatory letter), so the root proper is रेप्. Adding ल्युँट् replaces ल्यु with अन (ल् and ट् are dropped as anubandhas, and यु becomes अन by यु/वु → अन). This gives रेप् + अन. The न then becomes ण by "रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे", because the intervening प् (a पवर्ग letter) does not block the change. The result is the neuter noun stem रेपण (nominative रेपणम्).

<answer>रेपण</answer>

I read the verb as अस् (असँ, "to go, shine, take"), where the final anunāsika marker is dropped as an anubandha. This is a Bhvadi root with no prefixes. I assumed the root takes the connecting vowel इ before तृच्, which gives the agent-noun suffix -तृ. Adding it to the bare root gives अस् + इतृ. Because the root has a short अ and no guṇa or vṛddhi applies, the stem is असितृ.

<answer>असितृ</answer>

I read the root as जभ् with only the nasal marker ँ, which is not the ई that triggers the नुम् insertion. On that reading, the class 1 present stem is जभ + अ (शप्), and the शतृँ suffix gives the stem जभत्. The source might instead intend जभी, which would give जम्भत्, but I followed the citation as written.

<answer>जभत्</answer>

Here the verb is Curadi षद, which takes the causative-type suffix णिच्.

1. The initial ष् becomes स्, giving सद्.
2. Before णिच्, the vowel takes vṛddhi, giving साद्.
3. णिच् is then elided before the suffix यत् (since यत् is अनिट्), leaving साद्य.
4. The prefix आङ् is added in front. आ does not trigger retroflexion, so स् stays.

The stem is आसाद्य.

<answer>आसाद्य</answer>

Here is the derivation:

- The root मीङ् (class 4, "to hurt") takes the suffix अनीयर्, which is an ārdhadhātuka suffix and is not kit or ṅit.
- The ātva rule (6.1.50) names मीनाति with its श्ना vikaraṇa. I read that as limiting it to the class 9 root मीञ्, so it does not apply to the class 4 मीङ्. I am not fully certain of this reading.
- With no ātva, the final ई takes guṇa and becomes ए.
- That ए then becomes अय् before the vowel (मे + अनीय → मयनीय).

<answer>मयनीय</answer>

I formed it by treating मी (class 10, "to go") as taking the causative-type suffix णिच्, as Curādi roots do, and then adding क्त्वा. I derived this from memory of the rules and did not check it against a source.

1. Before णिच्, the vowel ई takes vṛddhi and becomes ऐ. Then ऐ followed by इ becomes आय्, giving मायि.
2. The thematic form of the stem is मायय्.
3. क्त्वा takes the augment इट्, becoming इत्वा. Because the suffix therefore begins with इ, णिच् is not dropped.
4. Joining the stem and suffix gives मायय् + इत्वा = माययित्वा.

<answer>माययित्वा</answer>

Using the root गुज् (class 1, "to hum or buzz") with the infinitive suffix तुमुँन् (तुम्), I treated it as a set root, so the iṭ augment (इ) comes between the root and the suffix. I did not settle whether the anunāsika marker on गुजँ makes the root anit instead. If it did, the form would be गोक्तुम्. I chose the set reading because it matches the usual गुजितुम्-type forms I recall for this root.

1. The suffix तुमुँन् reduces to तुम् once the anubandhas are dropped.
2. With the iṭ augment, the suffix is added as गुज् + इ + तुम्.
3. The root vowel उ is a short penultimate vowel, so it takes guṇa and becomes ओ (गु → गो).
4. This gives गोजितुम्.

<answer>गोजितुम्</answer>

The root is खोर् (the final ऋँ is only an anubandha marker), meaning "to obstruct movement". Adding ल्युँट् replaces यु with अन, which gives खोर् + अन. Because the न follows र, it becomes ण by the rule रषाभ्यां नो णः, so the stem is खोरण.

<answer>खोरण</answer>

The root is शर्व् (class 1, "to injure"), and the suffix ण्यत् leaves -य after dropping the markers ण् and त्. Because the suffix carries ण्, it would normally trigger vṛddhi of a penultimate short अ under the rule अत उपधायाः. Here the penultimate sound of शर्व् is र्, not a vowel, so no vṛddhi applies. The stem is therefore शर्व्य.

<answer>शर्व्य</answer>

This is an unverified derivation. The root is घुष् (घुषिँर्, class 1). The suffix क्त्वा is added with the connecting vowel इ, since the root is सेट्. By the rule "न क्त्वा सेट्", क्त्वा is normally not कित् after a सेट् root, so the root vowel takes guṇa: घुष् → घोष्, giving घोषित्वा. A second form, घुषित्वा, may also be valid under the optional rule रलो व्युपधाद्धलादेः संश्च. I give only घोषित्वा.

<answer>घोषित्वा</answer>

The root इविँ (class 1, "to pervade") carries the इत् marker इँ, so it takes the nasal infix (इदितो नुम् धातोः) and becomes इन्व्. Class 1 adds the vikarana शप् (अ), giving इन्व + अ. The शतृँ suffix then reduces to अत्, which yields the present active participle stem इन्वत्. Its strong stem is इन्वन्त्, but the base stem is इन्वत्.

<answer>इन्वत्</answer>

The root श्रा takes the suffix यत् by "अचो यत्" (3.1.97), since it ends in a vowel. Before यत्, the final आ of the root becomes ई by "ईद्यति" (6.4.65). Because the suffix is ārdhadhātuka, the ई then takes guṇa and becomes ए (7.3.84). This is the same pattern that gives देय from दा and पेय from पा. So श्रा + य gives श्रेय.

<answer>श्रेय</answer>

The root is क्रदिँ, and the इँ marker makes it इदित्, so it takes the nasal insertion (नुम्) and becomes क्रन्द्. It is a seṭ root, so the agent suffix तृच् (stem ending -तृ) joins with the connecting vowel इ. This gives क्रन्द् + इ + तृ, so the stem is क्रन्दितृ.

<answer>क्रन्दितृ</answer>

The root दाण् (दाने, class 1) is a ghu-root because it is not दाप् or दैप्. Before the nishtha suffix क्तवतु, "दो दद् घोः" (7.4.46) replaces its stem with दद्, which gives दद् + तवत् → दत्तवत्.

<answer>दत्तवत्</answer>

Sources differ on whether the anunāsika on उभँ affects the suffix, and I could not settle that from memory, so I treated it as irrelevant here.

The root उभ् (ubh) is seṭ, so क्त्वा takes the connecting इ, giving उभ् + इत्वा.

Rule 1.2.18 (न क्त्वा सेट्) says क्त्वा is not kit after a seṭ root, so it does not block guṇa. Rule 1.2.26, which can make क्त्वा optionally kit, applies only to roots beginning with a consonant, and उभ् begins with a vowel.

Guṇa of the penultimate short उ therefore applies, giving ओभ्, and the form is ओभित्वा.

<answer>ओभित्वा</answer>

Since the root is Curādi, it takes the causative-type suffix ṇic (*puṭ* + ṇic), and ṇic triggers guṇa of the penultimate short *u*, giving *poṭi*. The resulting stem ends in a vowel, so yat applies by "aco yat" (3.1.97). Before yat, ṇic is elided by "ṇer aniṭi", and the guṇa remains. This gives *poṭ* + *ya*.

<answer>पोट्य</answer>

I formed this by hand, starting from the root तृह् (class 7, "to injure"). I could not tell whether the citation form carries the ऊदित् marker that gives the optional इट्. Either way, तर्हित्वा is a valid form.

1. Added क्त्वा (a plain त्वा) with the connecting इट् to the root: तृह् + इ + त्वा.
2. क्त्वा after a root that takes इट् is not treated as कित् (rule "न क्त्वा सेट्"), so the root vowel ऋ takes guṇa and becomes अर्: तर्ह्.
3. The result is तर्हित्वा.

If the root is read as ऊदित्, the non-इट् alternative is तॄढ्वा, but I chose the इट् form.

<answer>तर्हित्वा</answer>

The root is पिष् (class 7, "to grind, crush"), which does not take the connecting vowel इट् (it is aniṭ). The suffix तृच् is added with guna of the root vowel, so इ becomes ए, giving पेष् + तृ. The ष् followed by त् becomes ष्ट, so the agent-noun stem is पेष्टृ.

<answer>पेष्टृ</answer>

Following the Dhatupatha entry, the class-10 root डप् takes the causative-type suffix णिच्. The penultimate vowel is lengthened by "अत उपधायाः", giving डाप् + इ = डापि. The suffix क्त then comes with the connecting vowel इट्, giving डापित.

<answer>डापित</answer>

The citation अद्टँ looks like a typo for अट्टँ, but I followed the supplied form as written. I derived the form in three steps:

1. Dropping the anubandha ँ leaves the root अद्ट.
2. As a Curādi (class 10) root it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving the stem अद्टि-.
3. Adding क्तवतुँ with the connecting इ gives अद्टितवतु, and the uninflected stem is अद्टितवत्.

If the root is actually अट्ट, the answer would instead be अट्टितवत्.

<answer>अद्टितवत्</answer>

This is a derivation from the class 2 root कु (kauti, "to sound"), with the suffix ल्युँट्.

1. ल्युँट् leaves the suffix यु after the anubandhas are dropped, and यु is replaced by अन (युवोरनाकौ, Pāṇini 7.1.1).
2. The suffix is not marked कित् or ङित्, so the final उ of the root takes guṇa, giving ओ.
3. Before the vowel of अन, ओ becomes अव्, giving कव् + अन.

The result is कवन.

<answer>कवन</answer>

The Dhatupatha root जभिँ has an इ anubandha (इदित्), which inserts a nasal (इदितो नुम् धातोः), so the root becomes जम्भ्. As a Curadi root it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving जम्भि (stem जम्भय्). Adding तव्य with the connecting vowel इ gives जम्भयितव्य.

<answer>जम्भयितव्य</answer>

Taking ष् as an anubandha, the root is झॄ (jhṝ), "to age" (ष् marks the divadi group of ṣit roots). The suffix is क्त, whose only marker is the क्. I derived the form from memory of the grammar rather than checking a source.

1. Before a consonant-initial suffix, the final ॠ of the root becomes इर् (ऋत इद्धातोः). Then हलि च lengthens the इ, giving झीर्.
2. Roots ending in ॠ take न in place of the त of the निष्ठा suffix (रदाभ्यां निष्ठातो नः). This gives झीर्+न.
3. The र् before न causes ण (retroflexion), giving झीर्ण.

<answer>झीर्ण</answer>

This is a derivation from the root लाछिँ (लाछि, "to mark"), class 1.

1. The anubandha इँ marks the root as इदित्, so a nasal (नुम्) is inserted: लाछ् → लाञ्छ्. The छ् takes the palatal nasal ञ्.
2. The suffix ल्युँट् leaves ल्यु, and युवोरनाकौ replaces यु with अन. The suffix is added without a connecting vowel.
3. Adding अन to लाञ्छ् gives लाञ्छन.

<answer>लाञ्छन</answer>

I derived this from the root पिच्च् (Curadi) with the suffix क्त. I did not check the Dhatupatha entry directly, so the compulsory णिच् in step 1 is an assumption.

1. Curadi roots take णिच्, giving पिच्चि. I assumed the आधृषाद्वा option for optional णिच् does not apply to this root.
2. क्त takes the augment इट्. Because the suffix begins with इट्, the णि is not elided (णेरनिटि 6.4.51 does not apply). The णि therefore shows as गुण plus अय्, giving पिच्चय् + इत.
3. The result is the past participle stem पिच्चयित.

<answer>पिच्चयित</answer>

पूङ् (पू, "पवने") is an ātmanepada root of class 1. Its ङ् is only an anubandha marker, so the root is not ūdit and the optional इट् of 7.2.44 does not apply. The suffix तृच् loses its markers and leaves तृ. Since तृ is not kit, the root takes the default इट् and the final ऊ takes guṇa: पू → पो → पव् before the vowel. This gives पव् + इ + तृ, so the agent-noun stem is पवितृ.

<answer>पवितृ</answer>

I recalled the root's details from memory rather than checking the Dhatupatha text. छष् (हिंसायाम्) carries an anudātta marker on its vowel, so it is treated as aniṭ and takes no connecting इ. Adding तव्यत् (stem तव्य) gives छष् + तव्य. The ष् turns the following त into ट by ष्टुत्व, so the result is छष्टव्य.

<answer>छष्टव्य</answer>

The root is पिल् (class 10, "to throw"), a Curadi root, so the suffix णिच् is added before तृच्. The laghu penultimate इ then takes guṇa (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च गुणः), giving पेलि. The connecting vowel इट् is inserted before तृच्, so पेलि + इ + तृ gives पेलयितृ (the agent stem).

<answer>पेलयितृ</answer>
