I treated पृच् as seṭ (it is not among the aniṭ roots), so it takes the augment इट्, since तृ is an ārdhadhātuka suffix beginning with a consonant other than य. The ऋ of the root takes guṇa to अर्, giving पर्च् + इ + तृ. This is from my recollection of the aniṭ-root list and was not checked against a source.

<answer>पर्चितृ</answer>

I could not confirm one detail: whether the root's short अ stays short before the Curadi णिच्. I assumed it does, as in कथयति and गणयति, but did not settle it from a rule, and the vṛddhi form लाटयितव्य is possible.

Formation: लट् + णिच् → लटि- (stem लटय-), then + तव्यत् with the connecting इट्, giving लटयितव्य.

<answer>लटयितव्य</answer>

The root is अह् (the nasal marker only marks the final "a" as an it), a class 5 root meaning "to pervade".

I could not confirm from the Dhatupatha whether the root is set or anit. I treated it as set because it is a single-syllable root that does not appear in the standard lists of anit roots. If the root were in fact anit, the form would be आढवत् instead.

1. The suffix क्तवतुँ leaves the affix -तवत् after the it-markers are dropped.
2. This suffix begins with a consonant other than य, so it is a valādi ārdhadhātuka suffix and takes the augment इट् (by 7.2.35). That gives अह् + इ + तवत्.
3. The resulting form is अहितवत्, which is the uninflected stem, with no case ending.

<answer>अहितवत्</answer>

The root षटँ (ṣaṭ, class 1, "to form a part") begins with ष, which is replaced by स by "धात्वादेः षः सः", giving सट्. The शब्दकोश-style form below assumes the root is सेट् (takes the इट् augment). I could not confirm this from the accent of the root, so it rests on the pattern that final-ट् roots such as शट, वट and रट are all सेट्.

With क्त, the इट् augment is inserted, so सट् + इ + त gives सटित.

<answer>सटित</answer>

The root is आछिँ (आछ्), whose इ-anubandha marks it as इदित्, so it takes a nasal augment (नुम्) and becomes आञ्छ् (आञ्छति). Because the root is इदित्, the nasal is not dropped before the क्त suffix, which is a कित् suffix. The root is also सेट्, so the suffix takes the connecting इट्. This gives आञ्छ् + इ + त = आञ्छित.

<answer>आञ्छित</answer>

The root is शस् (शसुँ, class 1, "to injure"); the anubandha उँ drops out. The suffix ण्वुँल् becomes अक, since वु is replaced by अक and the ण् and ल् markers drop. The marker ण् triggers vṛddhi of the root vowel, so शस् becomes शास्. Adding अक gives शासक, and the uninflected stem is below.

<answer>शासक</answer>

I derived this by hand, working from the citation form to the gerundive, and I am not fully certain of the details of the root's anubandhas.

1. The initial ष् of the root becomes स् by the rule that replaces a root-initial ष with स (धात्वादेः षः सः), so the root is स्वक्क्.
2. The anunasika marker and the accent mark on the root's final element are anubandhas and are dropped. The accent mark (anudātta) only makes the root ātmanepadī and does not affect the suffix.
3. The root has a single vowel and an anudātta marker, so it takes no connecting इ (एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्). The suffix therefore attaches directly, with no connecting vowel.
4. The suffix तव्यत् loses its anubandha and becomes तव्य, giving स्वक्क् + तव्य = स्वक्क्तव्य.

<answer>स्वक्क्तव्य</answer>

The root is हुड् (the ऋ and ँ in हुडृँ are markers that drop out). Since हुड् is not among the aniṭ roots, I take it as seṭ, so the infinitive suffix तुमुँन् becomes -तुम् with the augment इट्, giving हुडितुम्. Because the suffix is not ṅit, the penultimate short उ takes guṇa (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य, 7.3.86), so उ becomes ओ.

<answer>होडितुम्</answer>

The Dhatupatha root षगेँ has the final एँ as an anubandha, so the root is षग्. The initial ष् becomes स् (धात्वादेः षः सः), giving सग्.

The root is single-syllabled and takes the intermediate इ (it is seṭ), so क्त्वा becomes त्वा with इट् added: सग् + इ + त्वा. Since क्त्वा after a seṭ root is not kit, there is no change to the root vowel, which is already short अ.

This gives सगित्वा. I settled the seṭ status from recalled analogues (for example sthag and lag take इ before क्त्वा) and did not check it against a source.

<answer>सगित्वा</answer>

I formed the stem as follows. The Curadi root पुट takes the suffix णिच् (ṇic), and the penultimate short उ undergoes guṇa under Pāṇini 7.3.86, giving पोटि-. Adding तव्य with the connecting इ gives पोटयितव्य.

<answer>पोटयितव्य</answer>

This is my best reading of the entry, and it rests on two judgements I could not fully confirm.

1. The root णिजिँ॒ becomes निज् (initial ण् becomes न्). Its ँ marks it as इदित्, so नुम् is inserted, giving निन्ज्, with the nasal becoming ञ् before ज्.
2. Its anudātta marker makes it सेट्, so इट् is inserted before तव्य. No guṇa applies, since the penultimate sound is the nasal rather than a short vowel.

I followed the table's citation, which marks the root as इदित्. The class label does not match the traditional listing: I recall णिजिँर् as a class 3 root, and a table-faithful reading was my only guide.

<answer>निञ्जितव्य</answer>

The root is दाप् (class 2, "to cut"). Its final प् is an indicatory letter, so the root is दा. Adding ल्युँट् replaces ल् and ट् with nothing, and यु becomes अन (by युवोरनाकौ), so दा + अन gives दान. The uninflected neuter stem is दान.

<answer>दान</answer>

I read रविँ as the root रव् plus the anubandha इँ, which marks it as इदित्. The steps are:

1. For an इदित् root, नुम् is inserted after the last vowel (इदितो नुम् धातोः), giving रन्व्.
2. The suffix क्त becomes त, and the root is सेट्, so इट् is added, giving रन्व् + इत.
3. The nasal stays as न्. It becomes an anusvara or a homorganic nasal only before a झल् letter, and व् is not one. It also stays before क्त because the rule dropping the nasal does not apply to इदित् roots.

<answer>रन्वित</answer>

Since कुस्म् is in the Curādi class, it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving the stem कुस्मि. The final अ of कुस्म is dropped before णिच्. Then ण्वुल् replaces वु with अक. Before this अक, णिच् is dropped by "णेरनिटि". No vṛddhi applies. The upadhā of कुस्म् is स्, not अ, and the final letter is a consonant. The result is the stem कुस्मक.

<answer>कुस्मक</answer>

Forming the gerundive of the Curadi root ग्राम (ग्रामँ आमन्त्रणे):

1. The Curadi root takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving ग्रामि.
2. The stem now ends in a vowel, so अचो यत् (3.1.97) allows the suffix यत्.
3. Before यत्, the णिच् is elided by णेरनिटि (6.4.51), leaving ग्राम् + य.
4. The medial आ is already long, so no vṛddhi applies. The result is ग्राम्य, meaning "to be addressed".

<answer>ग्राम्य</answer>

I read the root as पिजिँ, with the इ anubandha, so it takes a nasal insertion and becomes पिञ्ज्. As a class 10 verb it takes णिच् and शप्, giving पिञ्जयति. Adding शतृँ gives the stem पिञ्जयत्.

<answer>पिञ्जयत्</answer>

The root धूञ् (धू, class 5, "to shake") takes ण्वुल्. The ण् and ल् are dropped as markers, and वु is replaced by अक by the rule युवोरनाकौ (7.1.1). Because the suffix carries ण्, the root's final ऊ takes vṛddhi and becomes औ, which becomes आव् before the vowel: धू + अक → धौ + अक → धावक. Since वु is already replaced by अक, no इट् is added.

<answer>धावक</answer>

The Dhatupatha entry is "अम द्रम हम्म मीमृँ गतौ…". Here the final anunāsika ऋँ is only an it-marker (under the rule उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत्), so the actual root is मीम्. This root is not in the list of aniT (non-इट्) roots, so it takes the connecting vowel इ before तव्य. The root's vowel ई is already long, so no guṇa applies. The suffix तव्यत् loses its marker त् and becomes तव्य, giving मीम् + इ + तव्य = मीमितव्य.

I reasoned this from memory of the Dhatupatha and the aniT list, not from a checked source.

<answer>मीमितव्य</answer>

The form below is my best derivation, but I am not certain it is right. The root is व्री, with the suffix क्तवतु (the past active participle suffix). My derivation assumes व्री is not in the ल्वादि group of roots that take न in the participle (Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.2.44), so the suffix takes the plain त form, and I could not confirm that. If व्री were in that group, the form would instead be व्रीणवत्.

1. Add the suffix: व्री + तवत् (क्तवतु).
2. Because I assume no natva applies, the त stays.
3. The uninflected stem is therefore व्रीतवत्.

<answer>व्रीतवत्</answer>

I did not work through the full derivation. Applying the suffix ल्युँट्, the यु becomes अन. The root's vowel is a short अ, so no guṇa or vṛddhi changes occur, and ध्रज् + अन gives ध्रजन.

<answer>ध्रजन</answer>

I read the root as सन्केत, a Curadi verb meaning "to summon," which takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving सङ्केतयति. Adding ल्युँट् turns the suffix into -अन, and the णिच् vowel drops before it. The nasal assimilates to ङ्, which yields the stem सङ्केतन (neuter form सङ्केतनम्). I worked this from memory of the Dhatupatha and did not check the entry against a source.

<answer>सङ्केतन</answer>

The root is मिल्, class 6, with the meaning "to join" (श्लेषणे). The suffix ल्युँट् leaves ल्यु after dropping the markers ल् and ट्, and ल्यु becomes अन (यु → अन by 7.1.1).

ल्युट् is not ङित् and counts as an आर्धधातुक suffix. So the short इ before a single final consonant takes guṇa (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च, 7.3.86): मिल् → मेल्. This gives मेल् + अन = मेलन.

I am not fully certain that मिल् lies outside the कुटादि group. If it were in that group it would be ङित्, guṇa would be blocked, and the form would be मिलन. I went with मेलन because मिल् forms its perfect as मिमेल, which points to a non-ङित् root.

<answer>मेलन</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, and I am not fully certain of the vowel length in the stem. The root is शम् (Curadi, meaning "to see, observe"). In class 10 it takes the णिच् (ṇic) suffix, giving the stem शामि-. The medial अ is lengthened by "अत उपधायाः". I take the "मितां ह्रस्वः" shortening not to apply here, because the root means "to see". This matches the attested निशामयति. The suffix क्त्वा then adds इट्, giving शामयित्वा. There is no prefix, so ल्यप् does not replace क्त्वा.

<answer>शामयित्वा</answer>

The root is बुस् (Divadi, "to emit/discharge"). The anunasika on the final vowel marks that vowel as an anubandha, so the base is बुस्. The suffix अनीयर् takes its final र् as an anubandha, leaving अनीय. It is ārdhadhātuka and not ङित् or कित्, so the root's ु takes guṇa: बुस् → बोस्. Adding अनीय gives बोसनीय, and the class-4 य-infix does not appear before an ārdhadhātuka suffix.

<answer>बोसनीय</answer>

The root is हय् (class 1, "to go"). The final nasalised vowel in the citation form is an anubandha and is dropped, leaving हय्. I assumed the root takes the augment इट् before क्त, so it forms हयित. I did not confirm this against the Dhatupatha accent marking, so the इट् assumption is not verified.

<answer>हयित</answer>

Applying ल्युँट् to व्रुडँ gives:

- The suffix ल्युँट् reduces to ल्यु, which becomes अन (by यु‑वुनोः अनाकौ).
- The root's उ takes guṇa to ओ, because ल्युँट् is an ārdhadhātuka suffix and is not कित् or ङित्.
- Result: व्रुड् + अन → व्रोडन.

<answer>व्रोडन</answer>

In the Curādi class the root मृग् takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving मृगि. The suffix ल्युँट् becomes ल्यु, which is replaced by अन. Because अन takes the augment इट्, णिच् is not dropped before it, and the guṇa of णिच् gives मृगय + अन. The न then becomes ण under the rule ऋवर्णान्नस्य णत्वम्, since only letters that do not block the change come between ऋ and न. This gives the stem मृगयण (neuter form मृगयणम्).

<answer>मृगयण</answer>

Following the convention for these tables, I give the bare stem rather than an inflected form.

The root is घष् (ghaṣ). Its anudātta marking (घषँ॒) means it takes the connecting vowel इ (it is seṭ). The suffix क्तवतुँ reduces to -तवत् once the anubandhas are dropped. This gives घष् + इ + तवत् = घषितवत्.

<answer>घषितवत्</answer>

The root is टुभ्लाशृँ, which reduces to भ्लाश् once the anubandhas (टु and ऋँ) are removed. Its meaning is "to shine" (दीप्तौ). The suffix ल्युँट् leaves यु after the markers ल् and ट् drop, and यु becomes अन by the rule that replaces यु with अन. This gives भ्लाश् + अन = भ्लाशन. The root needs no guṇa or other change before the suffix.

<answer>भ्लाशन</answer>

This is a derivation from the root क्षि॒ (class 6) with the suffix तृच्, whose anubandha च् drops. The root carries an anudātta accent and is a single syllable, so by the rule एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात् (7.2.10) it takes no इट् augment. The root vowel इ then takes guṇa before the ārdhadhātuka suffix, giving क्षे + तृ.

<answer>क्षेतृ</answer>

I formed this by hand from the Dhatupatha entry, without checking a source.

1. The initial ण् of the root becomes न् by the rule णो नः, giving नीव्.
2. The marker ँ makes the root इदित्, so a nasal is inserted by इदितो नुम् धातोः. This gives नीन्व्, parallel to तिवँ → तिन्वति.
3. I take the root to be सेट्, since it carries no marker making it अनिट्. So क्त्वा takes the connecting इ, giving नीन्व् + इ + त्वा.
4. Because the root is सेट्, क्त्वा is not कित् (न क्त्वा सेट्). The long ई is heavy, so no guṇa applies either, and the form is नीन्वित्वा.

<answer>नीन्वित्वा</answer>

कमुँ (कम्, "to desire") ends in the labial म् and has short अ as its penultimate vowel. Because of this, पोरदुपधात् (3.1.98) gives the suffix यत् rather than ण्यत्. Since यत् is not ञित् or णित्, there is no vṛddhi, so the form is कम् + य = कम्य.

<answer>कम्य</answer>

I derived the form by hand and did not check it against a reference text.

The root पि is marked anudatta, which makes it seṭ, so इट् is inserted before क्त्वा (त्वा). The rule "न क्त्वा सेट्" (1.2.18) makes क्त्वा non-kit after a seṭ root. Guṇa is therefore not blocked, and the final इ becomes ए. Then ए becomes अय् before the vowel of इत्वा. So पि + इत्वा gives पे + इत्वा, which gives पयित्वा.

The rule 7.2.11 that withholds इट् before a kit suffix applies only to श्रि and roots ending in उ, ऊ, ऋ, ॠ or लृ, so it does not apply to पि.

<answer>पयित्वा</answer>

I read the root as अङ्क (Dhatupatha अकि, with the nasal as an anubandha), class 10, "to mark; to be a sign". I formed it from memory of the usual forms, not from a checked source.

1. In class 10 the root takes the suffix णिच्, giving अङ्कयति. I recall causatives like कथयति and गणयति showing no vṛddhi of the medial अ, and I take अङ्कयति to behave the same way.
2. The suffix अनीयर् is added to the णिच् stem. The अय of णिच् is dropped before this ārdhadhātuka suffix, leaving अङ्क + अनीय.
3. The result is the gerundive stem अङ्कनीय.

<answer>अङ्कनीय</answer>

The root is कुप् (कुपँ, "to be angry"). The suffix ल्युँट् becomes यु after dropping the indicatory letters ल् and ट्, and यु is replaced by अन (युवोरनाकौ). The vowel उ of the root takes guṇa (ओ) before this suffix, so the stem is कोपन. The class-4 marker श्यन् is not added before a kṛt suffix.

<answer>कोपन</answer>

Following the supplied citation, the root लकँ (curādi, आस्वादने) takes the causative-type suffix णिच्. The anunasika on the final अ marks it as an a-final root of the kind that forms कथयति and गणयति. Its final अ is dropped before णिच्, and the penultimate अ is not given vṛddhi. This gives the stem लकि (as in लकयति). The suffix क्तवतुँ then becomes -वत्, with the connecting इ added, giving लकित + वत्.

I did not confirm the no-vṛddhi step against a source. It rests on the pattern of कथयति and गणयति as I remember them.

<answer>लकितवत्</answer>

The root is जम् (जमुँ, "to eat"). The उँ is an anubandha that marks the root as उदित्. By the rule "स्वरतिसूतिसूयतिधूञूदितो वा" (7.2.44), such a root takes the इट् augment optionally before तव्यत्. I chose the form with इट्: जम् + इ + तव्य → जमितव्य. The other valid form, without इट्, would be जन्तव्य.

<answer>जमितव्य</answer>

I derived this from the grammar rules as I remember them, and I am not fully certain of the vowel changes in the middle steps, but I am confident of the standard form देय.

The root दो (class 4, "to cut") has its final -ो replaced by आ (दा), by the rule ādeca upadeśe 'śiti. It then takes यत् (aco yat), and the standard result for this root is देय.

<answer>देय</answer>

I formed this from the root वस् (class 2, "to wear or clothe"), which is ātmanepada as its anudātta marker shows. An anudātta root takes the augment इट्, so the suffix तव्यत् (final त् is only an anubandha, leaving तव्य) joins as -इतव्य. The vowel is short अ, so no guṇa applies. This gives वस् + इतव्य = वसितव्य.

<answer>वसितव्य</answer>

I could not verify this derivation against the Dhatupatha or Kashika. The root गुज् (class 6, "to sound") is not in the list of roots that reject the connecting vowel इ, so इट् is inserted before the suffix. The suffix क्तवतु becomes -वत् once its markers are removed. It is marked कित्, so the root takes no guna and stays गुज्. This gives गुज् + इ + वत् = गुजितवत्, which is the uninflected stem.

<answer>गुजितवत्</answer>

The root is kiṭ (भ्वादि, "to frighten"). It is not in the traditional list of aniṭ roots, so I take it as seṭ and the suffix takes the augment iṭ. Adding क्तवतु (after dropping the markers, तवत्) gives kiṭ + i + tavat. The uninflected stem is किटितवत्.

<answer>किटितवत्</answer>

Root अघिँ॒ (class 1) is an इदित् root, so it takes a nasal and becomes अङ्घ्. Its final consonant is घ्.

The root has a single vowel and carries the anudātta marker, so it is अनिट् by "एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्". The suffix तव्यत् therefore loses its त् and is added without the connecting इ, giving अङ्घ् + तव्य.

Because the root ends in the aspirated झष् consonant घ्, the following त becomes ध by "झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः". The घ् then becomes ग् by जश्त्व. The result is अङ्ग्धव्य.

<answer>अङ्ग्धव्य</answer>

I read the ँ on ड as a plain anubandha (an anunasika अ), not the इ of an इदित् root, so I did not insert a nasal (नुम्). The root is then बिड्.

The suffix तव्य is an ārdhadhātuka suffix and the root is set, so it takes the connecting इ. The root vowel इ is a light vowel (laghu) in the penultimate position, and तव्य is not कित् or ङित्. The vowel therefore takes guṇa, giving बेड्. That gives बेड् + इ + तव्य = बेडितव्य.

<answer>बेडितव्य</answer>

I formed it by adding णिच् to the Curadi root शूर्प (to measure), then the gerundive suffix अनीयर्.

1. शूर्प + णिच् gives the stem शूर्पि.
2. Before the ārdhadhātuka suffix अनीयर्, the इ takes guṇa, giving शूर्पे. This becomes शूर्पय् by ay-ādeśa.
3. शूर्पय् + अनीय gives शूर्पयनीय.
4. The न of the suffix follows र् with only प, अ and य between them, which do not block retroflexion. So it becomes ण, giving शूर्पयणीय.

<answer>शूर्पयणीय</answer>

The root is चद् (the ए and the accent mark are anubandhas and drop out). Adding अनीयर् (the र् is dropped) gives चद् + अनीय. The root has a short penultimate अ, so no guṇa applies. The suffix begins with a vowel, so no इट् is needed. The stem is चदनीय.

<answer>चदनीय</answer>

<answer>शर्धकः</answer>

Correction: the stem should be given without the case ending, so the final form is:

<answer>शर्धक</answer>

This form is derived from the root मृष् (the उ in मृषुँ is an anubandha and drops). I could not confirm the iṭ treatment of this root against a source, so the form rests on the default assumption that it is seṭ.

1. The क्त suffix becomes त after dropping the anubandha क्.
2. The root is treated as seṭ, so the connecting vowel इ is inserted before त.
3. क्त is kit, so guṇa of the root vowel is blocked and ऋ stays.
4. The result is मृष् + इ + त = मृषित.

<answer>मृषित</answer>

The root is शिष् (Curadi), so the सार्वधातुक-type ṇic (णिच्) is added first. The vowel takes guṇa, giving शेषि. The suffix तव्यत् (तव्य) then follows with the connecting इ, which gives शेषयितव्य.

<answer>शेषयितव्य</answer>

Following the usual derivation, the root is first extended with the causative suffix णिच् (as is regular for Curadi roots), giving बस्तय-. The suffix ल्युँट् then replaces यु with अन, and the णिच् is elided before it. This yields बस्तन, a neuter noun stem.

<answer>बस्तन</answer>

Ṇic after ह्रप् gives ह्रपय-, and शतृँ (-अत्) then gives the stem ह्रपयत्. I assumed the root takes no upadha vṛddhi, as with कथयति and गणयति. I did not confirm this against the Dhatupatha or Kaumudi, so the alternative ह्रापयत् remains a possibility.

<answer>ह्रपयत्</answer>

The root is बुक्क् (class 10, "to bark"), and class 10 roots take the णिच् stem suffix. Before ण्वुल्, whose वु becomes अक, the णिच् is dropped. The upadhā of बुक्क् is a consonant, so no vṛddhi applies. The result is बुक्क् + अक = बुक्कक.

<answer>बुक्कक</answer>

This is a derivation from the Dhatupatha root कर्ज (class 1, "to pain") with the suffix ण्यत्. I derived it by hand and am not fully certain of the final consonant.

1. After removing the anubandha markers, the root is कर्ज and the suffix is -य. The ण् of ण्यत् is an indicatory letter that triggers vṛddhi, but it has no effect here. The vṛddhi rule (अत उपधायाः) applies only to a short अ in the penultimate position, and the penultimate sound in कर्ज is र्, not a vowel.
2. Under चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोः, a final ज of the root becomes ग before ण्यत्. This gives कर्ग्य. I found no exception that blocks this rule for this root. A form like कर्ज्य would be possible only if an exception applied, as may be the case with the similar word वर्ज्य.

<answer>कर्ग्य</answer>

Applying ण्यत् to the root भक्ष् (class 1) gives a ṇit suffix, so the penultimate short अ takes vṛddhi by "अत उपधायाः". The result is भाक्ष्य. Since the class given is 1, there is no णिच् to drop, which is what would otherwise yield भक्ष्य.

<answer>भाक्ष्य</answer>

I derived this by hand and did not check it against a source. I assumed the anunāsika marker on लडँ does not change the suffix-handling, so this is the best reading rather than a certain one.

1. The root is लड्, a class 10 (Curādi) verb, so the suffix णिच् is added: लड् + णिच्.
2. The penultimate अ takes vṛddhi before णिच् (Pāṇini 7.2.116), giving लाडि.
3. The infinitive suffix तुमुँन् (becoming तुम्) takes the connecting vowel इ, as the stem is a सेट् (iṭ-taking) stem, and the णिच् stem takes अय्: लाडय् + इ + तुम्.

The resulting infinitive is लाडयितुम्.

<answer>लाडयितुम्</answer>

Deriving the stem from मृषुँ (mṛṣ) with क्तवतुँ:

1. The anubandhas ु and ँ drop, leaving the root मृष्, and क्तवतुँ becomes the suffix -तवत्.
2. The root is seṭ, so इट् is inserted before the suffix. I assumed here that the optional इट् for udit roots (7.2.56) applies only to क्त्वा, so 7.2.15 does not block इट् for क्त and क्तवतु.
3. क्तवतु is kit (it has the anubandha क्), so guṇa of the root vowel ऋ is blocked.
4. This gives मृष् + इत + वत् = मृषितवत्.

I am not fully certain about the इट् step; the alternative would be a guṇa form such as मर्षितवत्, but I went with the kit-based form.

<answer>मृषितवत्</answer>

Following the standard rules, the root कृड् ends in a consonant and is not on the list of roots that refuse the iṭ augment, so it takes iṭ before तव्य. The suffix तव्य is not कित् or ङित्, so the short ṛ in the root's penultimate position takes guṇa under पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च. This gives कृड् + इतव्य → कर्डितव्य.

<answer>कर्डितव्य</answer>

The verb is लुठँ॒, which is anudātta (marked ॒) and so counts as aniṭ under 7.2.10 (एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्). The suffix क्त reduces to त, so no इ is inserted: लुठ् + त.

- By ष्टुना ष्टुः (8.4.41), त becomes ट, giving लुठ्ट.
- By खरि च (8.4.55), ठ् becomes ट्, giving लुट्ट.
- The optional single-letter reduction in 8.4.65 does not apply, because the ठ् is preceded by a vowel rather than a consonant.

I am not fully certain of this. A commonly attested form is लुठित, which would be correct if the verb were treated as set, but the anudātta marker points to the aniṭ derivation above.

<answer>लुट्ट</answer>

The root is ओँलजीँ॒, with the anubandhas ओँ (ओदित्) and ईँ (ईदित्), leaving लज्. The accent mark on the ī shows the root is anudātta. A single-syllable anudātta root takes no इट् before तव्य, so no connecting vowel is inserted.

तव्य is not कित्, so there is no guṇa change, and the short a of लज् stays. The final ज् becomes क् before the hard consonant त by चोः कुः. This gives लज् + तव्य → लक्तव्य.

<answer>लक्तव्य</answer>

This is the agent noun from the root नॄ with तृच्. The suffix तृच् is not a कित् or ङित् suffix, so the root vowel takes guṇa, giving नर्-. The rule वृतो वा (7.2.38) makes the इट् augment optional after roots ending in ॠ. That gives three valid stems: नर्तृ, नरितृ and नरीतृ. I chose the one with short इ.

<answer>नरितृ</answer>

This is a derivation from the root √इ (इक्, "to remember"), taken with the prefix अधि.

1. The suffix ण्वुल् has ण् as its marker, and वु is replaced by अक. The ण् marker triggers vṛddhi of the root vowel, so इ becomes ऐ.
2. Before the vowel of अक, ऐ becomes आय्, which gives the stem आयक.
3. Adding the prefix, अधि + आयक becomes अध्यायक by the इ → य् vowel sandhi.

<answer>अध्यायक</answer>

This form is derived from the root वृध् (वृधुँ), class 10, which takes the causative-type suffix णिच्. Guṇa gives the stem वर्धि. The absolutive suffix क्त्वा (त्वा) then attaches with the connecting vowel इ, and the णिच् stem shows as अय. No prefix is supplied, so ल्यप् does not apply.

<answer>वर्धयित्वा</answer>

I could not confirm whether this root takes the connecting vowel इ, so I assumed it does, by analogy with उष् (ओषिता). On that assumption the form is built as follows:

1. The root is व्युष् (the ँ only marks the anubandha). The suffix तव्यत् leaves तव्य after dropping its markers.
2. Because तव्य is ārdhadhātuka, the root vowel उ takes guṇa and becomes ओ, giving व्योष्.
3. With the connecting vowel इ added, the stem is व्योषितव्य.

<answer>व्योषितव्य</answer>

Forming the agent noun from ऋजिँ (ṛji, "to roast"):

1. The root is इदित् (it carries the marker इँ), so it takes the nuM augment (7.1.58). ṛji becomes ṛñj.
2. The suffix ण्वुँल् becomes अक, since वु is replaced by अक (7.1.1).
3. The suffix is ṇit, but no vṛddhi applies. Vṛddhi under 7.2.115 needs the vowel to be the final vowel of the base, and 7.2.116 only covers an upadhā short अ. Here ṛ is neither, because the nasal intervenes. The guṇa rule for a light penultimate vowel (7.3.86) also does not apply, because ṛ is not the upadhā.
4. The result is ṛñj + aka = ऋञ्जक.

This rests on my reading of how 7.2.115 treats the nuM-augmented base. I did not check it against a generated or attested form.

<answer>ऋञ्जक</answer>

Reading the root as चि (Curādi, "भाषायाम्") is a guess, since I could not match it to a specific Dhātupāṭha entry. Curādi roots take the causative-type suffix णिच्, so the steps are:

1. चि + णिच् → चै + इ, with vṛddhi of the root vowel before the ñit/ṇit suffix.
2. चै + इ → चाय् + इ, giving the stem चायि.
3. चायि + क्त (त) takes the augment इट्, giving चायित.

<answer>चायित</answer>

The root is तुहिँर् (तुह्), class 1, meaning "to hurt." The nasalized इँ marks it as इदित्, so it takes the नुम् augment, giving तुन्ह्. The अनुबन्ध इर् is dropped. I took the root to be सेट् (taking the connecting इ), since इदित् roots are generally सेट्; I did not check this against a source. Before the suffix तव्यत् the stem is therefore तुन्ह् + इ + तव्य. The नुम् nasal becomes anusvara before the झल् letter ह, giving तुंहितव्य.

<answer>तुंहितव्य</answer>

This is an assumption-based derivation, not a fully checked one. The root is कुर् (class 6, "to make a sound"), and the suffix क्त्वा becomes त्वा once its anubandhas drop.

The root is सेट्, so इट् is inserted, giving कुर् + इ + त्वा. Rule 1.2.26 (रलो व्युपधाद्धलादेः संश्च) optionally makes क्त्वा behave as कित् after a root with an इ/उ penultimate vowel, an initial consonant and a final र्. That optionality gives two valid forms, कुरित्वा without guṇa and कोरित्वा with guṇa. I chose the form without guṇa.

<answer>कुरित्वा</answer>

The root is इदित् (महिँ), so it takes the nasal augment (नुम्) and becomes मंह्. The anudātta marker (॒) shows it is सेट्, so the suffix तव्यत् takes the connecting इ. The suffix reduces to -तव्य, giving मंह् + इ + तव्य.

<answer>मंहितव्य</answer>

The root षुट्टँ becomes सुट्ट् (initial ष् → स् by धात्वादेः षः सः, and the final ँ is dropped as an anubandha). As a Curādi verb it takes णिच्, giving सुट्ट् + इ → सुट्टि with the stem form सुट्टय. The suffix तृच् then attaches with the connecting इट्, giving सुट्टय + इ + तृ. The uninflected agent-noun stem is सुट्टयितृ.

<answer>सुट्टयितृ</answer>

Working from the root उछ् (the ईँ is an it-marker), with ण्यत् added:

1. Before the suffix, तुक् is inserted after the short vowel before छ् (छे च), so उछ् becomes उच्छ्.
2. The suffix ण्यत् leaves य after dropping the markers ण् and त्.
3. No vṛddhi applies, because the root's vowel उ is initial and not a penultimate अ.
4. I assumed no इट् is added, treating the root as anudātta and single-syllabled. I also assumed the root-final छ् does not change to ष् under व्रश्च-भ्रस्ज…, since the छ् here comes from तुक्. I did not check either point against a source.

That gives उच्छ्य.

<answer>उच्छ्य</answer>

Adding ṇic to the Curādi root चट् gives चाटयति, with vṛddhi of the penultimate अ. Adding the suffix ल्युँट् then replaces ल्यु with अन, and the ṇic is dropped, which gives the neuter noun stem चाटन.

<answer>चाटन</answer>

कृपूँ (kṛp, "to be able") takes guṇa before तव्य, giving कृप् → कल्प्. By 8.2.18 the ṛ becomes ल in this root, so the stem is कल्प्. The root is ऊदित्, so 7.2.44 makes the इट् augment optional, and both कल्पितव्य and कल्प्तव्य are valid. I give the form with इट्.

<answer>कल्पितव्य</answer>

The root दहिँ has the anubandha इँ, which makes it इदित्, so it takes the nasal augment नुम्, giving दंह्. As a class 10 root it takes the suffix णिच्, giving दंहि-. The suffix क्त then takes the augment इट् and the णिच् is elided, which gives दंहित.

<answer>दंहित</answer>

Following the standard Pāṇinian derivation, I took the root as उध्रस् (class 10, "to glean"). The steps are:

1. Class 10 roots take the suffix णिच्. The penultimate अ takes vṛddhi (अत उपधायाः), giving उध्रास्, so the stem is उध्रासि and the finite form is उध्रासयति.
2. The suffix शानच् is used for the present active participle with ātmanepada formation. After शप् becomes अय, the stem ends in अ.
3. For such a stem, आने मुक् inserts म् before the suffix आन. This gives उध्रासय + मान.

<answer>उध्रासयमान</answer>

The root is पसिँ with the इँ anubandha, so it takes the infixed nasal (नुम्) and becomes पंस्. In class 10 it takes णिच् to give पंसि-, and शप् then gives the stem पंसय-. Adding शतृँ (अत्) forms the present active participle stem.

<answer>पंसयत्</answer>

I read the ँ on क्षलँ as marking an इदित् root, so I applied the rules in this order:

1. By 7.1.58, an इदित् root takes the nasal augment नुँम्, giving क्षन्ल्.
2. The नुँम् is not reduced before the क्त-type suffix, because 6.4.24 only removes it for roots that are not इदित्.
3. By 8.4.60 (तोर्लि), न् before ल् becomes a nasalised ल्ँ, giving क्षल्ँल्.
4. The root is set (takes इट्), so क्तवतुँ becomes -इतवत्, with the final stem form क्षल्ँलितवत्.

I am not certain about step 3. If the expected answer uses an anusvara instead of the nasalised ल्ँ, the form would be क्षंलितवत्. Also, I am assuming the given citation क्षलँ is correct as an इदित् root, and I did not check it against the Dhatupatha text.

<answer>क्षल्ँलितवत्</answer>

I derived this by working through the rules from memory rather than checking a reference, so it is the least certain step that decides the result.

The root ऋछ् takes the augment तुक् (6.1.73), giving ऋच्छ्. The suffix ण्वुँल् becomes अक. The ऋ is now followed by a conjunct, so it counts as heavy. Guṇa under 7.3.86 therefore does not apply, and vṛddhi under 7.2.115 does not apply either, since that rule affects only a final vowel. The ऋ stays unchanged, giving ऋच्छक.

<answer>ऋच्छक</answer>

The root is समीँ (Divadi, परिणामे). The ईँ is an anubandha, so the verbal base is सम्. I could not match this root to a verse I remember with confidence, so I treated it like मसी (the ई is an indicatory marker). The suffix तृच् is ārdhadhātuka and begins with a consonant, so it takes the augment इट् (सम् + इ + तृ). I did not find any rule that changes the root vowel here: the lengthening before श्यन् does not apply, and the ई marker only blocks इट् before the निष्ठा suffixes. Here `स्यमँ` (class 10, "to consider") takes the Curadi suffix `णिच्`, giving the stem `स्यमय-`. The root is ghaṭādi (`मित्`), so the vowel stays short. I am working from memory on this point; if the root were not `मित्`, the stem would be `स्यामय-` instead. `शानच्` then replaces `ल्` (Lat) in the ātmanepada, becoming `आन`. Because the stem ends in short `अ`, `मुक्` is added by `आने मुक्` (7.2.82), so `स्यमय` + `मान` gives `स्यमयमान`.

<answer>स्यमयमान</answer>

I worked this out from memory of the rules and could not check it against the Dhatupatha. I took रिहँ as an anit root, like लिहँ, because the ँ marker suggests no connecting ‑इ‑ is inserted. That is the main uncertainty.

1. The root is रिह्. The suffix तव्य is not कित् or ङित्, so the root vowel takes guna: इ becomes ए, giving रेह्.
2. The final ह् becomes ढ् before a त-initial suffix. This is the same pattern as लिह् → लेढा, लेढव्य.
3. The result is रेढव्य. If the root were seṭ, the form would instead be रेहितव्य.

<answer>रेढव्य</answer>

The root वृहँ (bṛh/vṛh) is anudātta (marked by ँ) and has one syllable, so by 7.2.10 it takes no connecting इ. Adding the past participle suffix क्त (त) gives वृह् + त. Then:

1. ह् becomes ढ् before त (8.2.31), giving वृढ् + ढ.
2. The first ढ् drops before the following ढ (8.3.13).
3. The vowel ऋ is not lengthened, because the lengthening rule for a dropped ढ/र (6.3.111) applies only to अ, इ, उ.

This yields वृढ. I am working from memory of the grammar rules, and I am fairly but not fully sure of this step-by-step derivation.

<answer>वृढ</answer>

This derivation is from memory and not checked against the Dhatupatha text. The root पथिँ (गतौ, class 10) has the इदित् marker, so it takes the नुम् augment (7.1.58) and becomes पन्थ्. As a Curadi root it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving पन्थि. The infinitive suffix तुमुँन् then adds इट्, giving पन्थयितुम्.

<answer>पन्थयितुम्</answer>

This is a derivation from the root तुन्प (tunp) with क्त्वा, as I worked it out by rule rather than checked against a source.

1. The root's nasal (न्) is part of the root itself. The anubandha is only the ँ marker, not an इ, so the root is not इदित्.
2. क्त्वा is a कित् suffix, and this root takes the connecting vowel इ (it is सेट्).
3. Rule 6.4.24 (अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति) deletes the penultimate nasal of a non-इदित् root before a कित् or ङित् suffix. This gives तुप् + इ + त्वा.

The result is तुपित्वा. I am less sure of this step: if the nasal were kept and assimilated instead, the form would be तुम्पित्वा.

<answer>तुपित्वा</answer>

I formed this from the root कुक् (class 1, "to take"), reading the accent mark in the citation as ātmanepada. I took it as a regular set (इट्-taking) root, so the suffix तव्य is added with the inserted इ. I did not settle what the candrabindu on the final क signals, but I believe it does not change this result.

<answer>कुकितव्य</answer>

I formed the stem by adding the causative/denominative suffix णिच् (the regular Curadi suffix) to मद्. The vowel in the middle of the root then takes vṛddhi, giving माद्‑अय‑. Adding the suffix तव्य with the connecting vowel इ gives the form below.

<answer>मादयितव्य</answer>

This is a derivation of the stem, taking the Curādi root as causative-type (णिच्) and attaching ल्युँट् (the ल्युट् suffix, which becomes अन).

1. The root अर्हँ (पूजायाम्) in class 10 takes णिच्, giving the base अर्हि.
2. ल्युँट् becomes ल्यु, which becomes अन after the anubandhas drop and यु is replaced by अन (युवोरनाकौ).
3. अन begins with a vowel, so no इट् is added. Before this अनिट् suffix the णिच् is dropped (णेरनिटि), leaving अर्ह् + अन.
4. The root's penultimate letter is र्, not अ, so no vṛddhi applies.
5. Retroflexion (णत्व) changes न to ण after र्, giving अर्हण.

<answer>अर्हण</answer>

Removing the anubandha ए (and the nasalisation ँ) leaves the root चत्. In the present, शप् gives the stem चत, and the शानच् ending becomes आन. Because the stem ends in short अ, the augment मुक् (7.2.82) is inserted before आन, giving चत + मान.

<answer>चतमान</answer>

The root is तन् (class 8, "to extend"). Before क्तवतु, the suffix is तवत्, since the क् and उ are markers that drop.

1. The root is marked with उ (तनुँ), so it has optional इट् in some contexts. Under "यस्य विभाषा" (7.2.15), this blocks इट् before क्त and क्तवतु.
2. The suffix क्तवतु is कित्, so the final न् of तन् is dropped before it. This follows the rule "अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनाम् अनुनासिकलोपो झलि क्ङिति", giving त + तवत्.
3. The result is the stem ततवत्. Its masculine strong stem would be ततवन्त्, but I give the base stem.

<answer>ततवत्</answer>

This is a judgment call between two forms. The regular क्त form of क्षुभ् with the इट् augment would be क्षुभित. Pāṇini 7.2.18 lists क्षुब्ध as a special form, but only when the sense is "churned" (मन्थ) and in a few other listed senses, and this meaning, सञ्चलने, is not among them. I chose क्षुब्ध anyway because it is the standard attested word for "agitated" (as in क्षुब्धः समुद्रः), and I could not confirm which form the table's source intends.

<answer>क्षुब्ध</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, and I did not check it against a source.

1. The root ह्वृ is a single-syllable root with an anudātta marker, so it takes no इट् before क्त (rule 7.2.10).
2. The ending -ṛ becomes -ir before the कित् suffix (7.1.100), giving ह्विर्.
3. The vowel lengthens before a following consonant (8.2.77), giving ह्वीर्.
4. After a root ending in र्, the initial त of क्त becomes न (8.2.42), and the न then becomes ण (8.4.1), giving ह्वीर्ण.

<answer>ह्वीर्ण</answer>

The root ज्रि is Curādi (class 10), so it takes the suffix णिच्.

1. ज्रि + णिच्: the णित् suffix causes vṛddhi of the root vowel, giving ज्रै + इ, which becomes ज्राय् + इ, i.e. ज्रायि.
2. The suffix यत् (अचो यत्) is added to this stem.
3. णेरनिटि removes the णिच् before यत्, which has no इट्. The vṛddhi stays, so the result is ज्राय् + य.

This gives ज्राय्य. I derived it by analogy with the parallel formation of चाय्य and did not check it against a cited form of ज्रि.

<answer>ज्राय्य</answer>

This is my best reading of the root's set/anit status, which I could not confirm from the supplied data.

The root is खुर् (tudādi). The suffix क्त reduces to the bare suffix त. I judge the root to be सेट् (taking the connecting vowel इ), so the form is खुर् + इ + त = खुरित.

<answer>खुरित</answer>

The root चक्षिँङ् (class 2, "to speak clearly") is replaced by ख्या before an ārdhadhātuka suffix (चक्षिङः ख्याञ्, 2.4.54). Before the yat-type suffix ण्यत्, the final आ of ख्या becomes ई (ईद्यति, 6.4.65). Guṇa then gives ए, so ख्या + ण्यत् → ख्येय. I did not check this against a derivation tool, and the ordering of ईद्यति against the yuk-augment rule (7.3.33) is the point I am least sure of. The result matches the familiar parallels देय, ध्येय and गेय.

<answer>ख्येय</answer>

The root अज् (class 1, गतिक्षेपणयोः) is replaced by वी before an ārdhadhātuka suffix, except before घञ् and अप् (Pāṇini 2.4.56). तुमुन् is an ārdhadhātuka suffix, so the root becomes वी. The root वी takes no इट् augment, so guṇa gives वे and the form is वे + तुम् = वेतुम्. I am recalling the rule and the aniṭ status of वी from memory rather than checking a source.

<answer>वेतुम्</answer>

I formed this by treating the root as स्खदिँर्, where the इँ marker makes it इदित्. I did not check the Dhatupatha entry itself.

1. Under 7.1.58 (इदितो नुम् धातोः), an इदित् root takes the नुँम् augment after its last vowel, so स्खद् becomes स्खन्द्.
2. The suffix ण्वुँल् reduces to वु after dropping its markers. Under 7.1.1 (युवोरनाकौ), वु is replaced by अक.
3. The medial अ of the root takes no vṛddhi, so स्खन्द् + अक gives स्खन्दक.

<answer>स्खन्दक</answer>

I took the root as ऋज् (ṛj), with the nasal anubandha removed. The suffix ण्वुल् becomes वु, and वु is replaced by अक. The ण् marker (ṇit) triggers vṛddhi of the penultimate short vowel, so ऋ becomes आर्. The final ज् stays unchanged, giving ऋज् + अक = आर्जक.

<answer>आर्जक</answer>

The root कुभिँ has an इ-anubandha, so it takes the नुम् augment and becomes कुम्भ्. As a Curadi root it takes the णिच् affix, giving कुम्भि. Adding क्त (which becomes त) with the connecting इ gives the participle stem कुम्भित.

<answer>कुम्भित</answer>

The root अठिँ (aṭhi, "to go") has the anubandha इँ, which makes it इदित्, so it takes the nasal augment नुम्: अठ् → अन्ठ्. The न् becomes ण् before the retroflex ठ् by ष्टुना ष्टुः, giving अण्ठ्.

The root is seṭ, so the suffix क्तवतु takes the augment इ: अण्ठ् + इ + तवत् = अण्ठितवत्. This is the uninflected stem.

<answer>अण्ठितवत्</answer>

This is my derivation of the form. I read the root as वुस्, with the anunasika marker (ँ) as the anubandha. Since it has no ending that forces aniṭ, it takes the connecting इट्.

The suffix तुमुँन् reduces to तुम् once its anubandhas (the initial त of the citation is part of the suffix, and ँ and न् drop). Because तुम् is ārdhadhātuka but not kit, the short penultimate उ takes guṇa (उ → ओ). This gives वुस् → वोस्, and then वोस् + इ + तुम्.

I did not check the Dhatupatha entry independently, so the class and meaning are taken from the table.

<answer>वोसितुम्</answer>

The root is रुट् (ruṭ), class 1, ātmanepadī. It is not in the list of aniṭ roots, so the suffix takes the connecting vowel इ. The suffix तव्यत् has no कित् or ङित् marker, so the root vowel takes guṇa: उ becomes ओ. This gives रोट् + इतव्य, which is रोटितव्य.

<answer>रोटितव्य</answer>

Following the Dhatupatha entry, the root is बिड् ("to cry out, abuse"). I took the final ँ to be the marker on the vowel, not the इ of an इदित् root, so no नुम् is added.

The suffix क्तवतुँ loses its markers and leaves -तवत्. Nothing in the standard list of anit roots covers a root ending in ड्, so I treated बिड् as seṭ, which means the connecting इ is inserted. That gives बिड् + इ + तवत् = बिडितवत्. I am inferring the seṭ status from that list, not from an explicit rule.

<answer>बिडितवत्</answer>

This is a derivation from the root as cited, not a check against the Dhatupatha itself.

1. The root is षस्तिँ, where the final इँ is an anubandha, so the base is षस्त्. The initial ष् becomes स् (षो सः), giving सस्त्.
2. Because of the इँ marker, the root takes the nasal augment (इदितो नुम्), inserted after its last vowel: सन्स्त्.
3. The suffix ल्युँट् leaves अन (ल् and ट् are dropped, and यु becomes अन). This gives सन्स्त् + अन = सन्स्तन.
4. Before the sibilant स्, the न् becomes anusvara (नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि), giving संस्तन.

<answer>संस्तन</answer>

The root is शन्बँ (शम्ब्), Curādi, "to connect". In the Curādi class it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, which is retained before क्त्वा because there is no prefix. The णिच् gives शम्बि, and its vowel is guṇated to शम्बे, which becomes शम्बय् before the iṭ-augmented क्त्वा, giving शम्बयित्वा. The न् of the root is written as म् by the standard rules of nasal assimilation.

<answer>शम्बयित्वा</answer>

This is a derivation from the stated root and suffix, but I could not confirm the root's Dhatupatha entry. I identified the root only from the citation जृ॒ (class 1, meaning गतौ).

1. The anudātta mark on जृ॒ makes the root seṭ, so the suffix क्त्वा takes the augment इट्.
2. Because क्त्वा is seṭ here, it does not behave as कित् (न क्त्वा सेट्). The root vowel therefore takes guṇa, so जृ becomes जर्.
3. Adding the augment and the suffix gives जर् + इ + त्वा = जरित्वा.

A second form, जरीत्वा, is also possible, because the इट् may optionally be lengthened (वृतो वा). I give जरित्वा.

<answer>जरित्वा</answer>

The root रविँ has the इँ anubandha (इदित्), so it takes the नुम् augment (7.1.58), giving रन्व्. The suffix ण्वुँल् reduces to वु, which is replaced by अक (7.1.1). That gives रन्वक.

This is a reasoned application of the rules rather than a form I could confirm against a source. I could not verify this root's entry in the Dhatupatha. I also chose the spelling with न् rather than an anusvara (रंवक) because the task does not say which to use.

<answer>रन्वक</answer>

The root is त्वच् (to cover), which takes no इट् before क्त. Adding क्त gives त्वच् + त → त्वच्‌त. The final च् changes to क् before the following त by the rule चोः कुः, so the form is त्वक्त.

<answer>त्वक्त</answer>

This follows the standard rules for the root बाह् (bāh), with the final ऋँ as an anubandha. I did not check any of this against a Dhatupatha text.

1. The accent mark (anudātta) on बाह् means the root is aniṭ under "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt", so तव्य takes no connecting इ.
2. The final ह् becomes ढ् by "ho ḍhaḥ", giving बाढ् + तव्य.
3. The त of तव्य becomes ढ by ṣṭutva, giving बाढ् + ढव्य.
4. The first ढ् drops by "ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ". The preceding vowel is already long, so there is no further lengthening.

The result is बाढव्य.

<answer>बाढव्य</answer>

Applying ल्युँट् directly to the root gives कृ + ल्यु. The ल्यु is replaced by अन (युवोरनाकौ), and the ṅit-like markers drop out. The final ऋ of the root takes guṇa, giving कर्‑ + अन. The न then becomes ण by the rule that changes न to ण after ऋ or र. The result is the stem करण.

<answer>करण</answer>

I did not check the Dhatupatha entry itself; the derivation assumes the stated class and meaning.

1. As a Curadi root, पुथ् takes the suffix णिच्, and the penultimate short vowel takes guṇa (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च), giving पोथि.
2. The agent suffix ण्वुँल् reduces to वु, which becomes अक. The णिच् is dropped before it (णेरनिटि), but the guṇa remains.
3. The result is पोथ् + अक = पोथक.

<answer>पोथक</answer>

Applying the "आदेच उपदेशेऽशिति" rule, the root-final ऐ of खै becomes आ before the non-शित् suffix, giving खा. The suffix ल्युँट् reduces to यु, which is replaced by अन, so खा + अन gives खान.

<answer>खान</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, and I am not certain of the guṇa step. The root गृह (class 10, ग्रहणे) takes the causative-type suffix णिच् (-aya-), and then तृच् is added with the connecting vowel इ, giving गृहयितृ. I did not apply guṇa to the penultimate ऋ (which would give गर्हयितृ). My recollection is that the class 10 root गृह is cited as गृहयति/गृहयते, but I could not confirm this against the Dhatupatha or the Kāśikā.

<answer>गृहयितृ</answer>

The root is दृन्फ् (tudādi, उत्क्लेशे), and I took it as aniṭ because the anunāsika marker ँ is read as an anudātta anubandha on an ekāc root. This reading of the marker is my best judgement and not something I could confirm.

1. The suffix तृच् loses its anubandha letters and leaves तृ.
2. The root's only vowel is ऋ, and the letter before the final फ् is न्, not an ik vowel, so no guṇa applies.
3. Because the root is aniṭ, no इट् is inserted.
4. The result is दृन्फ्‌ + तृ. The फ् and त् are both unvoiced, so there is no assimilation between them.
5. The non-final न् before the jhal letter फ् becomes anusvāra (नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि), and the anusvāra then becomes म् by parasavarṇa.

This gives the stem दृम्फ्तृ.

<answer>दृम्फ्तृ</answer>

The root is येषृ (yeṣ), with the final ऋ as an anubandha marker. The suffix क्त reduces to त. The root has more than one syllable, so it takes the connecting इ (iṭ) and is seṭ. This gives yeṣ + i + ta = येषित. I did not check this against a grammar text or dictionary.

<answer>येषित</answer>

Starting from the root ॠ with क्त्वा, I derived the form as follows. I am not fully certain of the choice between the valid variants.

1. ॠ is a ṛ-ending root, so the suffix takes the augment इट्, giving ॠ + इत्वा.
2. By "न क्त्वा सेट्" (1.2.18), क्त्वा after a root that takes इट् is not treated as कित्, so the guṇa of the root vowel is not blocked.
3. ॠ therefore becomes अर्, giving अरित्वा.

Other forms are also valid. By "वृतो वा" the इट् may be lengthened, giving अरीत्वा. A form without इट् is also possible, giving ईर्त्वा. I chose अरित्वा.

<answer>अरित्वा</answer>

The root is तन्च् (class 7), so the suffix ण्यत् gives तन्च् + य.

1. The root is ऊदित्, but its optional इट् does not arise, because य is not a वल् consonant.
2. The nasal stays, because ण्यत् is neither कित् nor ङित्. The vowel अ is not the penultimate letter (the penultimate is न्), so there is no vṛddhi.
3. Kutva by "चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोः" turns the final च् into क्, giving तन्क्य.
4. The nasal assimilates to the following consonant, so न् becomes ङ्, giving तङ्क्य.

<answer>तङ्क्य</answer>

Following the table's data, I read रफँ as a root रफ् whose final अ (marked ँ) is an anubandha. It is not on the traditional list of aniṭ roots and has no ū-marker for an optional इट्, so क्त्वा takes the connecting इ (इट्). क्त्वा is a कित् suffix, so no guṇa occurs. The result is रफ् + इ + त्वा = रफित्वा. I could not verify the root against the Dhātupāṭha directly, so this rests on that reading of the markers.

<answer>रफित्वा</answer>

I read the root as रन्ध् (idit, so it takes the nasal infix) and formed the absolutive from its णिच् stem. Because the root belongs to class 10, णिच् gives रन्धि. The vowel before the final consonant is not a short अ, since the nasal न् stands in the penultimate position. So there is no vṛddhi. क्त्वा then takes the इट् augment, giving रन्धयित्वा, and ल्यप् does not apply because there is no prefix.

<answer>रन्धयित्वा</answer>

Because the ँ in खर्जँ marks the root's vowel as anudātta, the root is aniṭ. This is from memory of how Dhatupatha markers work, and I did not check it against a source. Since the root is aniṭ, क्त (त) is added without the inserted इ, so the sequence is खर्ज् + त. By चोः कुः, the ज् changes to क् before त. That gives खर्क्त.

<answer>खर्क्त</answer>

Taking the root रा (rā, "to give", class 2) with the agent suffix ण्वुल्:

1. The suffix ण्वुल् has its final ल् and the marker ण् dropped, and its वु is replaced by अक (by "yuvoranākau"). This leaves the suffix as अक.
2. Because the suffix carries the marker ण् (ṇit), a root ending in आ takes the augment युक् (Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.3.33).
3. This gives रा + य् + अक, which is रायक.

<answer>रायक</answer>

This is a standard application of the ण्वुल् rule, and I did not check it against a commentary.

1. ण्वुँल् reduces to वु, which is replaced by अक (युवोरनाकौ), so the suffix is अक. The ण् marker triggers vṛddhi only for a final vowel or a medial short अ, so it does nothing to घुण्.
2. The suffix is ārdhadhātuka and neither कित् nor ङित्, so the medial short उ takes guṇa (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च), giving घोण्. The final ण् is already present in the root.
3. घोण् + अक gives घोणक. A comparable form is बोधक from बुध्.

<answer>घोणक</answer>
