2. The ṇic-suffixed stem takes guṇa of the light penultimate vowel (उ → ओ), giving पोणि.
3. The suffix यत् is aniṭ, so ṇic is elided before it (ṇer aniṭi, 6.4.51). The guṇa remains.
4. The result is पोण् + य = पोण्य.

I am fairly but not completely sure about step 2: it rests on the elided ṇic still conditioning guṇa, as in चोर्य from चुर्. The other candidate, पुण्य, is the familiar word, but it comes from the tudādi root पुण, so I did not use it.

<answer>पोण्य</answer>

Here the root is मस् (the ई in मसीँ is an anubandha), with the sense "to change form." The suffix तृच् is added with the connecting vowel इ, since मस् is a one-syllable root ending in स् and not on the list of roots that refuse इट्. The class-4 vikaraṇa श्यन् is not inserted, because तृच् is not a sārvadhātuka suffix. The agent noun is therefore मसितृ. The medial अ is already short, so no guṇa changes it.

<answer>मसितृ</answer>

खुड् (तुदादि, कुटादिगण का धातु) के साथ तुमुँन् लगाने पर इट् का आगम होता है। कुटादि धातु होने के कारण "अञ्णिन्ङित्" से यह प्रत्यय ङित्वत् होता है, इसलिए उपधा के उकार को गुण नहीं होता। इससे खुडितुम् बनता है। (यह धातु कुटादिगण में है, यह मैंने स्मृति से माना है।)

<answer>खुडितुम्</answer>

I read पिठँ as the root piṭh (class 1). The ँ is only the Dhatupatha's marker on the final vowel and does not mark an anudātta accent, so I treat the root as set (it takes the connecting vowel इ). This is a judgement: if the root were instead anit, the result would differ. With the suffix क्तवतुँ, whose anubandhas drop to leave -तवत्, this gives पिठ् + इ + तवत् = पिठितवत्, which is the stem form of the past active participle.

<answer>पिठितवत्</answer>

The Dhatupatha entry शौटृँ means "to be proud" and is a class 1 root. Its anubandha markers (ऋ् and the nasal ँ) drop out, which leaves the root शौट्. The ँ marks the root as anudātta, so it is seṭ and takes the connecting vowel इ before the suffix. The suffix क्तवतुँ loses its markers and becomes तवतु, whose stem form is तवत्.

Combining these gives शौट् + इ + तवत् = शौटितवत्, the uninflected stem of the past active participle.

<answer>शौटितवत्</answer>

Since धूप् is a Curādi root, it takes the stem-forming suffix णिच् (इ) before the primary suffix: धूप् + णिच् → धूपि. The suffix तव्य takes the connecting vowel इ (इट्), which gives धूपि + इ + तव्य. Guṇa then turns the इ of णिच् into ए, and ए becomes अय्, so the result is धूपयितव्य.

<answer>धूपयितव्य</answer>

This form is derived from the root त्रुन्प् (ँ is only an anubandha), with the suffix क्त (त).

1. The suffix क्त is कित्, and the root's nasal is part of the root itself, not an इदित् marker. The root is therefore अनिदित्, so rule 6.4.24 drops the penultimate nasal, giving त्रुप्.
2. I take the root to be सेट्, because it is not in the traditional list of अनिट् roots. This is from memory of that list, not checked against the text. So इट् is inserted before त, giving त्रुप् + इत = त्रुपित.

<answer>त्रुपित</answer>

The root लटँ (class 10, "to speak") takes the causative-type suffix णिच्. Before it, the penultimate अ undergoes vṛddhi (अत उपधायाः), giving लाटि-. Before the suffix ल्युँट्, the णिच् is dropped (णेरनिटि). ल्युँट् becomes ल्यु, and ल्यु becomes अन (यु → अन), so the result is लाट् + अन = लाटन.

<answer>लाटन</answer>

The root is ह्मलँ (class 1, meaning "to move"). The final ँ marks it as इदित्, so the augment नुम् is added (7.1.58), giving ह्मन्ल्. The suffix क्तवतुँ loses its markers and becomes तवत्. The root is सेट्, so इ is inserted before the suffix: ह्मन्ल् + इतवत्.

Before ल, the न् of the augment becomes an anunasika ल (8.4.60, तोर्लि). I took the resulting stem as ह्मल्ँलितवत्. I am unsure of the conventional way to write this nasalised ल, so the spelling of that sequence is my best rendering.

<answer>ह्मल्ँलितवत्</answer>

This is a calculated form, since the supplied citation (पठ as a Curadi root) does not match the usual Dhatupatha entry, which lists पठ in class 1. Treating it as Curadi, the root takes णिच्, and the steps are:

1. पठ takes णिच् as a Curadi root.
2. The penultimate short अ undergoes vṛddhi (अत उपधायाः), giving पाठि.
3. The suffix तृच् is added with the connecting vowel इ (इट्), and णिच् becomes अय before it, so पाठ् + अय + इतृ gives पाठयितृ.

The uninflected stem is below.

<answer>पाठयितृ</answer>

I stripped the anubandhas ृ and ँ from the citation form लौडृँ, which leaves the root लौड्. I could not confirm this reading against the Dhatupatha, since the root may instead be लोड्. I followed the form given in the table.

The suffix क्तवतुँ loses its markers and becomes -तवत्. The root takes the connecting vowel इ before it, giving लौड् + इ + तवत् = लौडितवत्. The result is the uninflected stem; the masculine nominative singular would be लौडितवान्.

<answer>लौडितवत्</answer>

Here is the derivation. The root is पृष् (pṛṣ), and its उँ anubandha makes it उदित्. Rule 7.2.44 ("स्वरति-सूति-सूयति-धूञूदितो वा") therefore makes the इट् augment optional before क्त and क्तवतु. The क्तवतुँ suffix reduces to तवत्. With the augment, this gives पृषितवत्. Without it, it gives पृष्टवत् (the स् of the suffix and the ष् combine to ष्ट). Both are valid, so I give one.

<answer>पृषितवत्</answer>

Following the Dhātupāṭha entry वहिँ॒ (वृद्धौ), the इ marker (इदित्) inserts a nasal, giving the root वंह्. The root has two syllables in its listed form, so it takes the connecting vowel इ before the infinitive suffix तुमुँन् (तुम्). This gives वंह् + इ + तुम् = वंहितुम्. The nasal appears as anusvāra because it stands before ह्.

<answer>वंहितुम्</answer>

The root is पुण् (curādi), so the suffix णिच् is added. The root's short उ is a laghu-upadhā and takes guṇa before णिच् (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च), giving पोणि-. The suffix क्तवतु् then takes the इट् augment (आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः) and णिच् is dropped, but the guṇa stays. This gives पोणितवत्, a participle stem that has no case ending yet.

<answer>पोणितवत्</answer>

Form: दसँ (class 10) takes the causative-type suffix णिच् (Curādi roots take it as a rule). The anunāsika (ँ) is an it-marker and drops, leaving the root दस्.

1. Before णिच्, the penultimate अ undergoes vṛddhi (अत उपधायाः), giving दास्.
2. Adding णिच् gives दासि (dāsi), which patterns like a class 10 verb.
3. Before तुमुँन् the stem takes the connecting इ (इट्), giving दासयितुम्.

<answer>दासयितुम्</answer>

I read the citation as the root माह् with the anubandha ऋँ (the ṛ is an it-marker), meaning "to measure". I could not match it to a standard Dhatupatha entry, so this reading is a best guess.

1. माह् has a single vowel (ā), so it is an ekāc root. An ekāc root ending in ह् is aniṭ, so क्तवतु takes no इ.
2. Before त, the final ह् becomes ढ् (हो ढः), giving माढ् + तवत्.
3. The त then becomes ध by "झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः", and ष्टुत्व turns that ध into ढ.
4. The first ढ् drops by "ढो ढे लोपः", and the preceding ā is already long. The result is माढवत्.

<answer>माढवत्</answer>

I derived this form by applying the following rules:

- The marker इर् in बुधिँर् is treated as a whole (the vārttika "इर इत्संज्ञा वाच्या"), so there is no नुम् insertion. The root is therefore बुध्.
- The root is अनिट्, so तुमुँन् becomes तुम् with no इट् augment.
- The penultimate उ takes guṇa before the suffix, giving बोध्.
- The ध् of the root and the त् of the suffix combine by "झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः", giving द्ध.

So बुध् + तुम् → बोद्धुम्.

<answer>बोद्धुम्</answer>

Taking the root as लुप् (Divadi, 4th class, in the sense "to bewilder"), the suffix क्तवतुँ reduces to तवत्. I read the ँ marker on the root as showing the root is अनिट् (no connecting इ), so तवत् attaches directly: लुप् + तवत् = लुप्तवत्. This setness is from memory of the Dhatupatha marking and I did not verify it against the text; if the root were सेट् the form would be लुपितवत्.

<answer>लुप्तवत्</answer>

Following the citation, the root is षन्बँ (सन्ब्), class 10, with the ṣ becoming s and the final ँ dropped as an anubandha. Class 10 takes the णिच् suffix, which gives सन्बि. Adding क्तवतुँ (-तवत्) gives the stem सन्बितवत्. Within the word, न् before the झल् consonant ब् becomes anusvara by नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि, and then म् by parasavarṇa. This gives सम्बितवत्. I am assuming that sandhi rule applies inside the root. A form that keeps न् (सन्बितवत्) would also be defensible if the root is not treated that way.

<answer>सम्बितवत्</answer>

I formed this by taking the root as शुच्य्, with ईँ as the anubandha. I worked it out from memory of the Dhatupatha and Paninian rules, not from a source.

1. The ईँ marker only blocks the augment इट् before the participle suffixes क्त and क्तवतु. It has no effect before तृच्, so इट् is added: शुच्य् + इ + तृ.
2. The vowel उ is not the penultimate sound of the root, because the root ends in -च्य्. Guṇa therefore does not apply.

The agent-noun stem is thus शुच्यितृ (nominative singular शुच्यिता).

<answer>शुच्यितृ</answer>

The root जजिँ is an इदित् root, so it takes the nasal insertion (नुम्) by "इदितो नुम् धातोः". The nasal assimilates to the following ज्, giving जञ्ज्. The root is not in the list of अनिट् roots, so it is सेट् and the suffix तृच् takes the augment इट्. This gives जञ्ज् + इ + तृ, and the agent-noun stem is जञ्जितृ.

<answer>जञ्जितृ</answer>

I did not fully verify whether this root takes the connecting vowel इ before the suffix. I believe पुष् is anit (no इ), and I formed the word on that assumption. Class 4 पुष् takes guṇa before the तव्यत् suffix, giving पोष् + तव्य, and ष् + त becomes ष्ट.

<answer>पोष्टव्य</answer>

The root is एठँ (eṭh), a class 1 root meaning "to harass, trouble". The anubandha ँ on ठ marks the root as इदित्, so by इदितो नुम् धातोः (7.1.58) it takes the nasal augment नुम्. The root therefore becomes एन्ठ्, and the न् becomes ण् before the retroflex ठ्, giving एण्ठ्.

The suffix ण्वुल् is replaced by अक (वु becomes अक). No vṛddhi applies. The only vowel before the final consonant is ए, and the rule अत उपधायाः affects only a short अ.

The result is एण्ठ् + अक = एण्ठक.

<answer>एण्ठक</answer>

I could not verify from memory whether गृजँ is treated as set (takes the इ augment) or anit, so the choice below is my best judgement. I treated it as set, because it is not on the traditional list of anit roots, and applied the following steps.

1. The root गृज् takes the infinitive suffix तुम् (तुमुँन्).
2. The suffix is not a ञित्/णित्, but it is not ārdhadhātuka-excluded either, so it takes the इट् augment. This gives गृज् + इ + तुम्.
3. The suffix is not कित्/ङित्, so the root vowel ऋ takes guṇa and becomes अर्. This gives गर्ज् + इ + तुम्.
4. Joining the parts gives गर्जितुम्.

<answer>गर्जितुम्</answer>

The root is लज् (class 10), so it takes the णिच् suffix before the primary suffix. The penultimate अ takes vṛddhi by "अत उपधायाः", giving लाजि (stem लाजय्). ल्युँट् then replaces ल्यु with अन, and the णिच् is elided, which gives लाजन. The neuter noun is लाजनम्, and the uninflected stem is लाजन.

<answer>लाजनम्</answer>

I read the root as षन्ब (सन्ब after the initial ष् becomes स्) and added the causative-type णिच् that Curādi roots take. The stem is then सन्बि. The stem ends in a vowel, so the suffix यत् applies by "aco yat" (3.1.97).

Before यत् the णिच् is elided, giving सन्ब्य. The preceding न् is not an ik vowel, so there is no vṛddhi. Finally, न् before ब becomes anusvāra and then the parasavarṇa म्, giving सम्ब्य.

<answer>सम्ब्य</answer>

Verb: वस् (class 10, "to love, cut, take away") takes the Curadi stem-forming suffix णिच्, which triggers upadhā-vṛddhi: वस् → वासि. In the present, शप् gives the stem वासय. The Ātmanepada participle suffix शानच् then becomes आन with the मुक् augment, giving वासय + मान.

<answer>वासयमान</answer>

This is the root ऋछ् (ṛch, class 6, ṛcchati), which takes the gerundive suffix तव्य. I formed it from the standard Pāṇinian rules as I recall them, without checking a grammar.

1. The root is single-syllable and, as far as I recall, not in the list of roots that take the connecting vowel इ, so it is अनिट् and तव्य is added directly.
2. The ऋ before the suffix takes guṇa, giving अर्छ्.
3. The छ् is treated as ending in च्छ्, which is replaced by ष् (8.2.36), as in प्रच्छ् → प्रष्टव्य. This gives अर्ष्.
4. The ष् changes the suffix's त to ट, which gives अर्ष्टव्य.

<answer>अर्ष्टव्य</answer>

Since रभिँ is इदित् (the इ is an anubandha), it takes नुम् by the rule इदितो नुम् धातोः, so the root becomes रम्भ्. Adding अनीयर् (the र् is an anubandha and drops) gives रम्भ + अनीय. The न of the suffix is then retroched to ण, because र precedes it and only labials (म्, भ्) intervene.

<answer>रम्भणीय</answer>

The root is चर्च् (carc). The anunāsika vowel is an anubandha and drops off. The root is seT, since it is not in the list of aniT roots, so the suffix क्तवतु (ktavatu) reduces to -तवत् and takes the connecting इ. This gives चर्च् + इ + तवत् = चर्चितवत्, which is the stem before any case ending.

<answer>चर्चितवत्</answer>

This is my best derivation; I am not fully certain of the root's Dhatupatha details.

The root भजिँ is Curadi (class 10), so it takes the causal-type suffix णिच्. The anubandha इँ marks it as इदित्, so it takes the nasal insert नुम्, giving the base भञ्ज्. Vrddhi does not apply, because the penultimate sound is ञ्, not अ. Adding णिच् gives भञ्जि- (stem भञ्जय-). The suffix क्त्वा then takes the augment इट्, and with no verbal prefix it stays क्त्वा rather than becoming ल्यप्. The result is भञ्जयित्वा.

<answer>भञ्जयित्वा</answer>

This is a derivation from memory. I am unsure whether the root takes the connecting vowel इ before क्त्वा, so the answer rests on treating it as अनिट् without a firm check.

1. The root षुहँ becomes सुह्, since the initial ष् is replaced by स्.
2. Treating it as अनिट्, the suffix is added directly: सुह् + त्वा.
3. The final ह् becomes ढ् (हो ढः), and the त् of the suffix becomes ध्, giving सुढ् + ध्वा.
4. The ध् becomes ढ् after ढ्, giving सुढ्ढ्वा.
5. The first ढ् is dropped (ढो ढे लोपः), and the preceding उ is lengthened to ऊ (ढ्रलोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽणः).

This yields सूढ्वा.

<answer>सूढ्वा</answer>

I read the root as मेद् (the anubandha ऋँ is dropped) with the गुण vowel ए already present, so no vowel change applies. Adding the gerundive suffix अनीयर् (अनीय after the final र् is dropped) gives मेद + अनीय. The stem form is मेदनीय. I followed the Devanagari root exactly as supplied; the meaning given (मेधाहिंसनयोः सङ्गमे च) is the one usually attached to मेधृ, so if मेधृ was intended, the stem would be मेधनीय.

<answer>मेदनीय</answer>

This is a derivation from the root रुठ् in class 10 (Curādi), meaning "to speak" (भाषायाम्).

1. Curādi roots take the suffix णिच् (शप् is replaced by अय in the finite forms), so the stem is रुठ् + णिच्.
2. The root vowel उ is short and medial (लघूपध), so it takes guṇa before the ṇit suffix: उ → ओ (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य गुणः). This gives रोठि.
3. The suffix तव्य is an ārdhadhātuka suffix beginning with a consonant, so इट् is added: रोठ् + इ + तव्य.
4. The अय of णिच् is retained before इट्, giving रोठयितव्य.

<answer>रोठयितव्य</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, not checked against a source. The root गुण (class 10, आमन्त्रणे) takes the causative-type suffix णिच् (ṇic) as usual for Curadi roots, giving the stem गुणि. Before the ārdhadhātuka suffix यत्, ṇic is dropped by ṇeraniṭi (6.4.51), leaving गुण् + य = गुण्य. I did not apply guṇa to the root vowel, since गुणयति is the attested form (unlike चोरयति from चुर), though I could not fully confirm the rule behind this.

<answer>गुण्य</answer>

I derived the form below, but I am not certain it is correct: the root's anit status is my inference. I read the anunasika marker in अहँ as marking the root as anit, which means no इट् is inserted before तुमुँन्. This inference is uncertain; if the root were set, the form would be अहितुम्.

1. The root is अह्, and the suffix तुमुँन् leaves तुम्, giving अह् + तुम्.
2. Under हो ढः, the final ह् becomes ढ्.
3. Under झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः and ष्टुत्व, the त् of तुम् becomes ध् and then ढ्, giving अढ् + ढुम्.
4. Under ढो ढे लोपः, the first ढ् drops.
5. Under ढ्रलोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽणः, the preceding अ lengthens to आ.

<answer>आढुम्</answer>

The verb is अस् (class 2, "to be"). Before an ārdhadhātuka suffix such as क्तवतु, अस् is replaced by भू (अस्तेर्भूः, Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.4.52). Adding क्तवतु gives भू + तवत् = भूतवत्, the uninflected stem of the past active participle.

<answer>भूतवत्</answer>

The root is रु (class 1, ātmanepada, meaning "to go; to hurt"). It is a monosyllabic root ending in short -u, so it is aniṭ and the suffix क्त (-त) attaches without the connecting vowel इ. The root keeps its vowel unchanged, so the participle stem is रुत.

<answer>रुत</answer>

The root is दाप् (दा with the anubandha प्), so the base is दा, ending in ā. The suffix तव्यत् loses its markers (त् and अ's marker) and becomes तव्य. No guṇa applies to an ā-ending root, and no इट् is added, so दा + तव्य gives दातव्य.

<answer>दातव्य</answer>

I read the root as यौट् (the final ऋँ is only an anubandha), meaning "to bind". It is a single-syllable root ending in ट्, and it is not on the list of aniṭ roots, so it takes the इट् augment before क्त्वा. Because the suffix is not kit after a seṭ root (1.2.18), no change applies to the औ. This gives यौट् + इ + त्वा.

<answer>यौटित्वा</answer>

Taking the root as णीलँ (nīl, "to colour"), the initial ण् becomes न् by the rule णो नः, giving नील्. The suffix तृच् loses its markers and leaves तृ. The root is seṭ, so the augment इट् is added before it. The long ई is not changed, since guṇa applies only to a short penultimate vowel or a final vowel. This gives नील् + इ + तृ = नीलितृ. I did not treat the ँ as adding a nasal (num), because the attested forms of this root (नीलति, निनील) show none.

<answer>नीलितृ</answer>

This root is इक् (स्मरणे), whose final क् I am taking as a real consonant of the root rather than an indicatory letter. I am not certain of this point. The anudātta accent only marks the root as ātmanepada. The prefix is अधि, and अधि + इक् gives अधीक्. When a prefix is present, the absolutive suffix क्त्वा is replaced by ल्यप् (-य), which gives अधीक्य. If the क् were instead an anubandha, the form would be अधीत्य.

<answer>अधीक्य</answer>

I could not fully verify the root's anubandhas against the Dhatupatha. I took the final ल as part of the root, giving पल्यूल्.

1. The root is Curadi (class 10), so it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving the stem पल्यूलि.
2. The penultimate ऊ is already long, so there is no guna or vrddhi change.
3. Before the ardhadhatuka suffix यत्, the णिच् is elided, so पल्यूल् + य gives पल्यूल्य.

<answer>पल्यूल्य</answer>

Applying ण्यत् to the root चर्च् leaves the suffix as य (the ण् and त् are markers). The penultimate letter of चर्च् is र्, not a short अ, so the vṛddhi rule अत उपधायाः does not apply. The final च् changes to क् by चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोः. The exception list in 7.3.66 (यज, याच, रुच, प्रवच, ऋच) does not cover चर्च्, so the substitution applies. This gives चर्क्य. I did not find a worked example of this exact form, so the result rests on that reading of the rules.

<answer>चर्क्य</answer>

Here I take तृन्फँ to be the root तृफ् with a nasal written into it, class 6, with an anudātta anubandha (the ँ). I am working from memory of the Dhatupatha rather than a checked source.

1. The root is a single syllable with an anudātta marker, so it is अनिट् and क्त्वा takes no इट्.
2. क्त्वा is कित्, so there is no guṇa on ऋ.
3. For the same reason the nasal is dropped before the suffix (अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति), giving तृफ् + त्वा.

<answer>तृफ्त्वा</answer>

Taking the table's input as the verb घटिँ (class 10, "to speak"), I formed the agent noun in these steps:

1. The anubandha इँ marks the root as इदित्, so a nasal is inserted (7.1.58 इदितो नुम् धातोः). The root becomes घण्ट्.
2. As a Curadi verb it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, which gives the stem घण्टि.
3. The suffix तृच् is added with the connecting vowel इट्. This gives घण्ट् + अय + इ + तृ, which combines to घण्टयितृ.

The answer below is the uninflected stem, as requested; the nominative singular would be घण्टयिता.

<answer>घण्टयितृ</answer>

I did not verify the Dhātupāṭha accent marking for this root. I assumed it takes the connecting vowel इ before the तव्य suffix, so the form is ह्लस् + इ + तव्य.

<answer>ह्लसितव्य</answer>

The Dhatupatha root is णू (nū), class 6, "to praise". The initial ण् becomes न्, so the root is नू.

The suffix तव्यत् loses its markers and becomes तव्य, which is added to the guṇa-strengthened root (नू → नो, then नो + अव् → नव्). I treated this class 6 root as set (taking the inserted इ). The traditional list of anit roots in ऊ that includes "नौति" refers to the class 2 root, so I did not apply it here. This is my best judgement rather than a certain ruling.

नू + तव्य → नव् + इ + तव्य → नवितव्य

<answer>नवितव्य</answer>

I read the root as क्षीव्, with ऋ as a marker letter that drops out. Adding क्तवतु (ktavat) gives the participle. I did not run the derivation through a tool, so the choice of क्षीबवत् rests on my recollection of Pāṇini 8.2.55. That sūtra lists क्षीब as an irregular निष्ठा form. If I have recalled it correctly, the suffix takes no इट् and the root's व becomes ब. The 8.2.55 rule applies when no verbal prefix is present, as here. The uninflected stem is therefore क्षीबवत्.

<answer>क्षीबवत्</answer>

The root is मन् (मनुँ, class 8, "to understand"). The ending ु is the anubandha. The root is anudātta, so it takes no इट् before क्तवतु.

By अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनाम् (6.4.37), the final nasal of a tanādi root drops before a kit suffix beginning with a jhal consonant. This gives मन् + क्तवतु → म + तवतु → मतवत्.

<answer>मतवत्</answer>

The root is रक्ष् (class 1, "to protect"), and the suffix is अनीयर्. The final र् of the suffix is only an anubandha, so the suffix is added as अनीय.

The root is अनुदात्तेत्? रक्षँ has the marker ँ, which only marks the nasal. It is a plain parasmaipadī root, and the suffix is not marked with ङित् or कित्, so no guṇa is blocked. The root vowel is the short अ, which takes no guṇa or vṛddhi.

The thematic vowel अ of class 1 does not appear before this suffix, since kṛt suffixes do not take शप्. Adding the suffix directly gives रक्ष + अनीय = रक्षणीय.

Retroflexion of न् after ष् is not an issue here. The न् of अनीय follows रक्ष्, whose ष् is followed by अ. By the rule रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे, न् becomes ण् after र, ष, ऋ, or ॠ even when a vowel or other permitted sounds intervene. Here ष् is followed by अ and then न, so न becomes ण.

The result is रक्षणीय.

<answer>रक्षणीय</answer>

The root is ईर्क्ष्य् (the final anunasika is only a marker). It ends in a consonant, so ण्यत् applies by ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (3.1.124).

- No vṛddhi applies. The upadhā is ष्, which is not an इक् vowel, so 7.2.116 does not apply.
- No इट् is added, because the suffix य does not begin with a val consonant.

The result is ईर्क्ष्य् + य, which gives ईर्क्ष्य्य.

<answer>ईर्क्ष्य्य</answer>

The root is रिविँ (इदित्, Bhvadi, "to go"), so it takes the नुम् infix after its last vowel: रिवि → रिन्व्. The suffix ल्युँट् becomes अन (the ल्यु is replaced by अन, and the ट् and the nasal marker drop).

There is no guṇa, because the इ is not the final sound of the stem. The stem रिन्व् is followed by अन, giving रिन्वन.

The न of the suffix then becomes ण. The preceding र् still triggers retroflexion across the intervening इ, the नुम् nasal and व्, which Pāṇini 8.4.2 allows.

<answer>रिन्वणम्</answer>

Forming the gerundive from ह्वल् (class 1, "to move") with तव्य. This is from memory of the rules, and I am not fully certain of the root's status or of the sandhi.

1. The nasal marker ँ makes the root इदित्, so it takes the augment नुम् (7.1.58), giving ह्वन्ल्.
2. The root is सेट्, so the connecting vowel इ is inserted before तव्य, giving ह्वन्ल् + इतव्य.
3. The न् stands before ल, so it assimilates to a nasalised ल्ँ (8.4.60 तोर्लि).
4. Result: ह्वल्ँलितव्य.

The simpler spelling ह्वंलितव्य is also possible, but I have chosen the fully assimilated form.

<answer>ह्वल्ँलितव्य</answer>

This is formed from the root तस् (तसुँ, class 4, "to waste away"), with the suffix तृच् (तृ) giving an agent noun.

The suffix तृच् is an ārdhadhātuka suffix, so the root takes the connecting vowel इ. I judged the root to be seṭ because तस् does not appear in the list of aniṭ roots as I recall it, and the short उँ marker does not trigger an optional इट् here (that applies only before क्त्वा, 7.2.56).

The derivation is तस् + इ + तृ = तसितृ. The stem is given without case endings.

<answer>तसितृ</answer>

The root हुडिँ has the marker इँ, so the आगम नुम् is inserted (इदितो नुम् धातोः, 7.1.58). The nasal then assimilates to ण् before ड्, giving the root हुण्ड्. The root is anudātta, hence seṭ, so the suffix तव्य takes the augment इट्. This gives हुण्ड् + इ + तव्य = हुण्डितव्य.

<answer>हुण्डितव्य</answer>

The root is दुहिँर् (दुह्), class 1, in the sense "to afflict". Two anubandhas matter here. The इँ marks the root as इदित्, so a nasal नुम् is inserted (इदितो नुम् धातोः), giving दुन्ह्, which is written दुंह्. The इर् is dropped as a marker.

I took the root to be seṭ, so क्तवतु takes the connecting इ and gives दुंहितवत्. The aniṭ list cites the second-class root दुह्, which I judged not to cover this class-1 root. I am not fully certain of this step.

<answer>दुंहितवत्</answer>

The root दहिँ is इदित् (it carries the marker इँ), so it takes a nasal insertion (नुम्) and becomes दंह्. As a class 10 verb it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving दंहि. The suffix तव्यत् then attaches with the connecting vowel इट्, giving दंह + अय + इ + तव्य, which is दंहयितव्य.

<answer>दंहयितव्य</answer>

I take मसीँ to be the root मस् with ईँ as the anubandha. Because it is ईदित्, it takes no इडागम in the निष्ठा forms (7.2.14), but that rule does not extend to क्त्वा. The root is otherwise सेट्, so the absolutive takes इट् before क्त्वा (त्वा), giving मसित्वा. I derived this from the rules as I recall them, not from a lookup in the Dhatupatha or a commentary.

<answer>मसित्वा</answer>

The Dhatupatha root धि (Tudadi, "to hold") takes the suffix तृच्, which becomes तृ once the anubandha marks च् is dropped. The root's accent mark shows it is anudātta, so it is aniṭ and no इट् is inserted. The suffix is ārdhadhātuka, so the final इ of the root takes guṇa and becomes ए. This gives धे + तृ = धेतृ.

<answer>धेतृ</answer>

I treated the final इँ of त्वगिँ as an anubandha, which gives the root त्वग् and inserts the nasal (नुम्): त्वङ्ग्. I took the root as सेट् (taking the connecting इ), as with similar roots like लङ्घित and अङ्गित. I did not verify this against a source. Adding क्तवतुँ gives the past active participle stem त्वङ्गितवत्.

<answer>त्वङ्गितवत्</answer>

I formed this from the root as supplied, उर्ज (short u), with the ṇic of class 10 (curādi) and then the suffix तव्य.

1. The class 10 root takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, which becomes -अय-. This gives उर्जय-.
2. The suffix तव्य takes the connecting vowel इ. This gives उर्जयितव्य.

The stem vowel उ is followed by र्, so no guṇa or vṛddhi applies.

<answer>उर्जयितव्य</answer>

The root is भर्ब् (the nasalised अ in भर्बँ is only a marker and drops out), meaning "to go". The suffix ल्युँट् leaves ल्यु + ट्, and ल्यु becomes अन (यु → अन). Adding it gives भर्ब् + अन = भर्बन. The root already contains ऋ-grade र्, so no guṇa applies. Because र् precedes the न् with only ब् and अ between them, the rule रषाभ्यां नो णः turns न into ण. The stem is therefore भर्बण.

<answer>भर्बण</answer>

I formed this by hand from the root बिल् (the ँ is only a marker and is dropped) and the suffix तव्य (the ् of तव्यत् is dropped); I did not check it against a reference.

1. The suffix तव्यत् takes no विकरण, so there is no श in the class 6 form. The stem is बिल् + तव्य.
2. बिल् is a single-syllable root with no exemption from the connecting इ, so इट् is inserted: बिल् + इ + तव्य.
3. तव्य is an ārdhadhātuka suffix that is not ङित् or कित्. The medial short इ therefore takes guṇa, giving बेल्.
4. The result is बेलितव्य.

One point I was unsure of: if बिल् belonged to the कुटादि group, तव्यत् would act as ङित् and block guṇa, giving बिलितव्य. I could not place the root in that group from memory, so I went with the guṇa form.

<answer>बेलितव्य</answer>

The root is धूर् (the ईँ in धूरीँ is an anubandha, इर्, and drops). With क्त्वा, the rule रलो व्युपधाद्धलादेः संश्च makes the इट् augment optional, since the root ends in a consonant and has an इ/उ-type vowel in the penultimate position. So both धूरित्वा and धूर्त्वा are valid, and I give धूरित्वा.

<answer>धूरित्वा</answer>

The root मनुँ (class 8) has its final उँ as an anubandha, so the operative root is मन्. The suffix ण्वुँल् loses its markers: ण् and ल् drop as indicators, and वु becomes अक. Because the suffix carries ण्, the penultimate अ of the root takes vṛddhi (मन् → मान्). Adding अक gives मानक.

<answer>मानक</answer>

Stripping the anubandha ṛ from एषृ gives the root एष् (to go). The suffix ण्वुल् becomes अक, since वु is replaced by अक and the ण् and ल् are only markers. The ण् would trigger vṛddhi on a final vowel or a medial short अ, but the root ends in a consonant and its medial vowel is ए, so no vṛddhi applies. The result is एष् + अक = एषक.

<answer>एषक</answer>

I took the root as फेल् (the ऌँ is only an anubandha marker) and added क्त्वा, which becomes त्वा. The root is set, so इट् is inserted. फेल् has ए as its penultimate vowel, so the optional kit-rule for roots with penultimate इ or उ does not apply. This gives फेल् + इ + त्वा = फेलित्वा.

<answer>फेलित्वा</answer>

The root गृजिँ has an इ anubandha (इदित्), so it takes the नुँम् augment: गृ‑न्‑ज् → गृंज्, and the nasal becomes ञ् before ज्, giving गृञ्ज्. The suffix ल्युँट् becomes ल्यु, which is replaced by अन (the ल् and ट् are markers and यु → अन). The vowel ऋ is not in the penultimate position, because the nasal stands between it and the final consonant. So the guna rule for a light penultimate vowel does not apply and the ऋ stays. The result is गृञ्जन, and the uninflected stem is given.

<answer>गृञ्जन</answer>

The root गर्ज् (class 10, "to sound") takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, which is regular for Curādi roots, before the agent suffix.

1. ण्वुल् becomes अक, since ण् and ल् are markers and वु is replaced by अक.
2. णिच् is dropped before the अक suffix, leaving the stem गर्ज् + अक.
3. The suffix is marked ण्, so it would normally trigger vṛddhi. Neither vṛddhi rule applies here. The rule अत उपधायाः needs an अ as the penultimate sound, but the penultimate sound of गर्ज् is र्. The rule अचो ञ्णिति needs a final vowel, but the root ends in the consonant ज्.
4. The form is therefore गर्ज् + अक = गर्जक.

<answer>गर्जक</answer>

The root षुहँ (सुह्) is anudātta (the ँ marker), so it takes no इट्, and the suffix is तवत् after the anubandha is dropped. The derivation:

1. षुह् becomes सुह् (षः सः).
2. सुह् + तवत्: ह् becomes ढ् by हो ढः.
3. त becomes ध after ढ् by झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः, giving सुढ्‌धवत्.
4. The first ढ् is dropped by ढो ढे लोपः, and the preceding vowel lengthens by ठूलोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽणः, giving सूढवत्.

The ghatva option (वा द्रुहमुहष्णुहष्णिहाम्) does not apply, because सुह् is not in that list.

<answer>सूढवत्</answer>

I could not confirm the root's iṭ status from memory. I took the udātta mark (॑) in the citation to mean the root is aniṭ, so क्त्वा is added without the connecting इ. With ष् followed by त्व, the dental becomes retroflex (ष्टुत्व), so छष् + त्वा gives छष्ट्वा. If the root were actually seṭ, the form would instead be छषित्वा.

<answer>छष्ट्वा</answer>

The root तुर्वीँ has its final ईँ as an anubandha marker, so the root is तुर्व् (turv). In class 1 (Bhvadi) the present stem takes शप्, giving तुर्व + अ. The suffix शतृँ then leaves अत्, since the markers श and ऋ drop out. Together this gives तुर्व + अत् = तुर्वत्. The strong stem is तुर्वन्त्, but the uninflected base is तुर्वत्.

<answer>तुर्वत्</answer>

Curadi verbs take the suffix णिच्, so the derivation runs as follows.

1. चि + णिच् takes vrddhi of the root vowel (चै + इ), and ऐ becomes आय्, giving चायि (causative stem चाययति).
2. Adding क्त (the past participle suffix, which takes इट्) gives चायित.

An alternative form with आ and प्, चापित, is also valid under the optional rule चिस्फुरोर्णौ. I chose चायित.

<answer>चायित</answer>

The root is लौड् (the ऋँ is an anubandha). The suffix ण्वुँल् reduces to वु after dropping its markers, and वु is replaced by अक. The root vowel already carries vṛddhi (औ), so no further change applies. This gives लौड् + अक = लौडक.

<answer>लौडक</answer>

I read रोडृँ as the root रोड् (class 1, "to be mad"). Its ऋ and ँ are anubandhas, and the ँ marks it as anudātta. An ekāc anudātta root takes the augment इट्. Adding क्तवतुँ, whose उँ and क् drop, leaves the stem ending -वत्. This gives रोड् + इ + तवत्.

<answer>रोडितवत्</answer>

The root छदिँ has the इ anubandha, so it takes a nasal (नुम्) and becomes छन्द्. As a class 10 root it then takes the णिच् suffix, which gives छन्दि (stem छन्दय). The agent suffix तृच् is added with the connecting vowel इट्, which gives छन्दयितृ. The stem is given here in the form ending in ऋ, with no case ending.

<answer>छन्दयितृ</answer>

Assuming the final ँ on चीभृँ marks it as इदित् (इ-anubandha), I built the form from the root चीभृ with the following steps. I am not fully certain of this reading of the root.

1. The इदित् marker gives the आगम नुम् (इदितो नुम् धातोः), inserted after the last vowel, so the root becomes चीभृन्.
2. ल्युँट् leaves यु, which is replaced by अन (युवोरनाकौ), giving चीभृन् + अन.
3. The ऋ is now the upadha and is light, so it takes guṇa (अर्), giving चीभर्न् + अन.
4. The न् right after र् becomes ण् (रषाभ्यां नो णः), giving चीभर्ण् + अन. The second न stays, because the intervening ण् is not one of the letters that allow णत्व to carry through.

<answer>चीभर्णन</answer>

The root ष्टभिँ has the इ anubandha, so it takes a nasal augment (इदित्), and the initial ष् becomes स्. This gives the base स्तम्भ्. The suffix तव्यत् becomes तव्य, with the augment इ added because the root is treated as सेट्. This gives स्तम्भितव्य.

I am not fully certain the root is सेट्. The alternative would be an अनिट् form such as स्तब्धव्य, but I chose स्तम्भितव्य because the nasal would not normally be dropped before तव्य, and स्तम्भितव्य is the form I recall being attested.

<answer>स्तम्भितव्य</answer>

Since रघ is a Curādi root, it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, which gives रघ + णिच्. The णित् suffix lengthens the penultimate अ, so the stem becomes राघ् with the suffix इ, giving राघि.

The suffix क्तवतु (stem form वत्) begins with a consonant, so it takes the augment इट्. Adding it gives राघि + इत + वत्, which simplifies to राघितवत्.

<answer>राघितवत्</answer>

This is a derivation from the root as cited, and I am relying on my reading of the markers and rules rather than a checked source.

The ँ on शुन्धँ marks an अ-anubandha, so the root is ādit. Rule 7.2.16 (आदितश्च) therefore blocks the इट् augment before क्त and क्तवतु, which gives शुन्ध् + तवत्.

The root has no इदित् marker, so 6.4.24 (अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति) drops the nasal before the kit suffix, giving शुध् + तवत्.

By 8.2.40 (झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः) the त of the suffix becomes ध, giving शुध्धवत्. By 8.4.53 (झलां जश् झशि) the first ध् becomes द्, giving शुद्धवत्.

The participle takes the stem form ending in -वत्.

<answer>शुद्धवत्</answer>

This is an unverified judgement between two candidates. The root श्री (श्रीञ्, class 9, "to cook") with क्त would regularly give श्रीत. However, Pāṇini 6.1.27 (शृतं पाके) substitutes शृ before the निष्ठा suffix क्त when the meaning is "cooking", and the Kāśikā, as I recall it, includes श्रीञ् among the roots it covers. Since the given meaning is पाके, I chose the substituted form शृत, which I did not check against the text.

<answer>शृत</answer>

The root is मर्ब् (class 1, "to go"). The अँ after the final ब् is an anubandha that drops away, so there is no नुम् augment. The root is not among the अनिट् roots, so it takes the connecting इ before क्त. With क्त reduced to त, this gives मर्ब् + इ + त = मर्बित.

<answer>मर्बित</answer>

The root is तुस् (tus), which is not on Pāṇini's list of aniṭ roots, so क्तवतु takes the connecting vowel इ. That gives तुस् + इ + तवत् = तुसितवत्. This is the uninflected stem; the nominative masculine singular would be तुसितवान्.

<answer>तुसितवत्</answer>

The root षलँ (ṣal, "to go") begins with ष्, which is replaced by स् (धात्वादेः षः सः), so the root becomes सल्. It is not in the list of अनिट् roots, so it takes the connecting इ before तव्य, which gives सल् + इ + तव्य. The गुण substitution does not apply because the medial अ is already short.

<answer>सलितव्य</answer>

The root पडिँ is इदित्, so it takes a nasal insertion: पड् → पण्ड्. As a class 10 root it then takes णिच्, giving पण्डि. The suffix ण्यत् is added to this stem, and the णिच् is dropped before it by णेरनिटि, leaving पण्ड् + य.

I did not apply upadhā-vṛddhi to the root vowel. This follows the pattern of comparable class 10 gerundives such as कथ्य and गण्य, which I am relying on from memory rather than from a rule I could reconstruct here. The stem is therefore पण्ड्य.

<answer>पण्ड्य</answer>

This answer rests on how I read the accent marks, and I am not certain of it.

The root is विदॢँ (vid, class 6, "to obtain"). In the citation the vowel of वि is marked anudātta, which I took to mean the root is seṭ (it takes the connecting इ before the suffix). The ऌ and ँ are only anubandha markers and do not change the stem. The infixed न of the present stem (विन्दति) does not appear in this formation.

Adding तृच्, whose च् drops as an anubandha, gives विद् + तृ. The connecting इ gives विद् + इ + तृ. Guṇa of the root vowel then gives वेदितृ.

I also recall that dictionaries list a form वेत्तृ (vettṛ) for this root, which would follow if the root were aniṭ, so the seṭ reading is the uncertain step.

<answer>वेदितृ</answer>

I derived this by the usual rules, and the result depends on one reading of the input: that the ँ on नर्बँ marks the root as इदित् (taking the नुम् augment).

1. The ँ marks the root as इदित्, so नुम् is inserted after its last vowel (इदितो नुम् धातोः): नर्ब् → नन्र्ब्.
2. The root is सेट्, so the participle suffix क्त (→ त) takes the इट् augment.
3. The nasal is not dropped before the कित् suffix, because the elision rule applies only to non-इदित् roots.
4. The result is नन्र्ब् + इ + त = नन्र्बित, the stem of the past participle.

<answer>नन्र्बित</answer>

Applying "धात्वादेः षः सः" (A. 6.1.64), the initial ष् of षल् becomes स्, giving the root सल्. The suffix ल्युँट् reduces to यु after dropping the anubandhas, and "yu" is replaced by "ana" by "yuvoranākau" (A. 7.1.1). The root vowel takes no guṇa, so सल् + अन gives the stem सलन.

<answer>सलन</answer>

I treated the final ई of मदीँ as an anubandha that is dropped, leaving the root मद्. This ई does not trigger the nasal insertion (नुम्), which applies only to short इ-marked roots. Its only effect is on the past participle (निष्ठा), so it does not affect तव्य. The root is सेट्, so इट् is inserted before तव्य, and the vowel takes guṇa: मद् + इ + तव्य gives मदितव्य.

<answer>मदितव्य</answer>

Formation, from the root उख् with अनीयर्:

1. The root is उख्, which ends in a consonant, and the suffix अनीय begins with a vowel, so no इट् augment is needed.
2. The suffix अनीयर् is not ङित् or कित्, so the penultimate short उ takes guṇa under the rule पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च. This gives उ → ओ.
3. Adding the suffix gives ओख् + अनीय = ओखनीय.

I recall ओखति as the attested present form of this root, but I did not check it against a source.

<answer>ओखनीय</answer>

I formed this from the root यु (class 2, "mixing and separating") with the absolutive suffix क्त्वा, which becomes त्वा.

यु is one of the roots (यु, रु, क्ष्णु, शीङ्, स्नु, नु, क्षु, श्वि, डीङ्, श्रि, वृ) that are सेट्, so the suffix takes the augment इट्. Because क्त्वा after a सेट् root is not कित् (न क्त्वा सेट्), the root vowel takes गुण: यु → यो, and before the vowel of इट् this becomes यव्. The result is यव् + इ + त्वा = यवित्वा.

I recalled the सेट् status of यु from the traditional mnemonic verse, not from a source I checked here.

<answer>यवित्वा</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, not checked against the text of the Dhatupatha or the Ashtadhyayi.

The root दृन्फँ (class 6, "to be agitated or distressed") has the ँ as an anubandha, and the root itself is दृन्फ्. I take it to be seṭ, since it is not among the standard aniṭ roots. The suffix तव्यत् becomes तव्य, so the form is दृन्फ् + इ + तव्य.

- The suffix तव्यत् is not कित् or ङित्, so guṇa is possible. The ṛ is not the penultimate sound, however, because the nasal न् stands before फ्. Rule 7.3.86 therefore does not apply, and the ṛ stays unchanged.
- The न् stands before the sound फ् and becomes anusvāra by rule 8.3.24. This then becomes the nasal of the following sound's class, म्, by rule 8.4.58. The result is दृम्फितव्य.

<answer>दृम्फितव्य</answer>

Reading the citation as the root माह् (the ऋ and ँ are anubandhas that drop out), the suffix अनीयर् loses its markers and becomes -अनीय. The root's vowel is already long ā, and the final ह stays before a vowel, so no further change applies. This gives माह + अनीय = माहनीय. I am not certain of this reading of the citation, so the form rests on that assumption.

<answer>माहनीय</answer>

The root ष्टगेँ (ṣṭage, "to cover") loses its final anubandha ए, leaving ष्टग्. Its initial ष् becomes स् by the rule that a root-initial ष् turns into स्. This removes the trigger for ष्टुत्व (retroflexion of the following dental), so ट returns to त, giving स्तग्.

The suffix तव्यत् leaves तव्य after its anubandha is dropped. I treated the root as सेट् (it takes the connecting इ), which matches the familiar participle स्तगित. This was a judgment from memory, since I could not settle the accent of the anubandha. The vowel is not strengthened, so the stem is स्तग् + इ + तव्य.

<answer>स्तगितव्य</answer>

The root मदिँ has the anubandha इँ (इदित्), so it takes the num-augment and becomes मन्द्. The root is marked anudātta (मदिँ॒), so it is सेट् and takes the connecting इ before the infinitive suffix तुमुँन् (तुम्). This gives मन्द् + इ + तुम् = मन्दितुम्.

<answer>मन्दितुम्</answer>

This is a standard present active participle. The root णेदृँ॑ loses its anubandha ऋँ, leaving णेद्. The initial ण् becomes न् by the णोपदेश rule, so the root is नेद्. In class 1 the verbal stem takes शप् (अ) to give नेद, and the suffix शतृ then gives the participle stem नेदत्.

<answer>नेदत्</answer>

Reading the citation त्वगिँ as a root with the इ anubandha (इदित्), the nasal is inserted, giving त्वङ्ग्. Adding ल्युँट् (ल्यु becomes अन) gives त्वङ्ग् + अन = त्वङ्गन. No guṇa applies, and no इट् is inserted because the suffix begins with a vowel.

<answer>त्वङ्गन</answer>

I could not confirm from memory whether this root takes the augment इट्, so the answer rests on treating it as aniṭ.

1. The root is तुर् and the suffix is क्त, whose "त" remains after the markers are dropped. This gives तुर् + त.
2. Under रदाभ्यां निष्ठातो नः (8.2.42), the त of the निष्ठा suffix becomes ण after र्. This gives तुर्ण.
3. Under हलि च (8.2.77), the penultimate vowel उ of a root ending in र् is lengthened before a consonant. This gives तूर्ण.

If the root were seṭ, the result would instead be तुरित.

<answer>तूर्ण</answer>

This is a best-effort derivation, because I could not confirm every rule for this root.

The root ष्मिङ् becomes स्मि, since the initial ष् is replaced by स्. As a Curadi root it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्. I assumed the stem takes ā plus the pug augment, giving स्मापि. I am not certain of the exact rule; the alternative would be the guṇa form स्मयि. Adding तव्यत् and the connecting vowel इ gives स्मापयितव्य.

<answer>स्मापयितव्य</answer>

The root is एज् (the ऋ in एजृँ is an anubandha marker and drops out). Adding ल्युँट् gives the suffix अन, with ल् and ट् as markers and यु replaced by अन. The vowel ए is already a guṇa vowel, so no further change applies. The result is एजन, the uninflected stem (neuter nominative singular एजनम्).

<answer>एजन</answer>

The root is हुडिँ (huḍi, "to collect"). Its इँ (anubandha) marks it as इदित्, so a nasal नुम् is inserted: हुड् → हुनड् → हुं‌ड्. The nasal then assimilates to the following ड् as ण्, giving हुण्ड्.

अनीयर् begins with a vowel, so no इट् is added. Its अ is the actual suffix, and the final र् is only an anubandha. The result is हुण्ड् + अनीय = हुण्डनीय.

<answer>हुण्डनीय</answer>

I formed this from the root √छद् (class 10, "to cover, conceal") by hand, and I'm not fully certain about the vowel. Adding the class-10 suffix णिच् gives छादि- with vṛddhi of the penultimate vowel. Adding क्त with the augment इ gives छादित. I did not settle whether the anunasika marker on the root could instead signal a short-vowel form, छदित.

<answer>छादित</answer>

Following the table, the root गुपँ॒ is a single-syllable root marked anudātta, so rule 7.2.10 (एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्) bars the इट् augment before क्त. The suffix क्त reduces to त, which gives गुप् + त = गुप्त.

<answer>गुप्त</answer>

The citation णिदृँ॑ has ṛ as an anubandha, so the root is णिद् (ṇid), and the initial ण् becomes न् by the ṇopadeśa rule. The root has no nasal insertion. Before the suffix अनीयर् (anīya), the i of the root takes guṇa, giving नेद् + अनीय. I read the ṛ as an anubandha rather than a nasal-bearing इदित् marker; the citation as printed could also be read as a corrupted णिदिँ, which would give निन्दनीय.

<answer>नेदनीय</answer>

The root is षलृँ, where the ऌ is only an anubandha marker, so the root is षल्. By the rule धात्वादेः षः सः, the initial ष् becomes स्, giving सल्. The suffix तव्यत् leaves तव्य after its markers are dropped. The root takes the connecting इट्, so सल् + इ + तव्य gives सलितव्य. The vowel of सल् is अ, so no guṇa applies.

<answer>सलितव्य</answer>

This is a derivation from the rules as I recall them, not checked against a source, and I am unsure of two steps.

1. The root जिरि has the final इ as an anubandha marker (इदित्), so the bare root is जिर्.
2. The rule इदितो नुम् धातोः inserts a nasal after the last vowel, giving जिन्र्. I kept the nasal as न् rather than writing an anusvara. The rule that turns न् into an anusvara applies only before झल् consonants, and र is not one. This is the step I am least sure of, since a source might write the anusvara form जिंरितव्य instead.
3. I treated the root as सेट्, because it ends in र् and is not in the aniṭ list, so the suffix takes इट्: जिन्र् + इ + तव्य.
4. The suffix तव्य is not ङित् or कित्, but no guṇa applies anyway: the final consonant र् stands between the इ and the suffix. The result is जिन्रितव्य.

<answer>जिन्रितव्य</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, and I am not fully certain of it. I am unsure whether guṇa applies to this root.

The root कुह् is Curādi, so it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, giving कुहि. The short उ in the penultimate position takes guṇa (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च), giving कोहि. The suffix यत् is anit, so णि is dropped before it (णेरनिटि). This leaves कोह् + य.

<answer>कोह्य</answer>

The Dhatupatha root is दैप् (शोधने), with the final प् as an anubandha, so the root is effectively दै. Before the non-ित् suffix तव्यत् (stem ending -तव्य), its ऐ becomes आ by the rule "आदेच उपदेशेऽशिति", giving दा. The root is monosyllabic and ends in a vowel, so it is अनिट् and takes no इट् augment. Adding तव्य gives the stem दातव्य.

<answer>दातव्य</answer>

The root is कुन्चँ (kuñc), class 1, with the nasal न् as part of the root and no इ-anubandha, so it is अनिदित्.

1. The suffix क्तवतुँ becomes -तवत् after the markers are dropped. It is कित्, and the root is सेट्, so इट् is inserted: कुन्च् + इतवत्.
2. By अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति (6.4.24), the penultimate nasal is dropped before a कित् or ङित् suffix: कुच् + इतवत्.
3. The result is the stem कुचितवत्.

I did not find a rule that blocks the nasal-drop here (6.4.30 applies only to अञ्च्). I could not confirm the point against a Dhatupatha source. The usual form कुञ्चित suggests a variant with the nasal retained, but I followed the rule as stated.

<answer>कुचितवत्</answer>

I took the root as होड् (ṛ is the anubandha) and the suffix क्त as plain त after dropping the anubandha क्. The root is ekāc, but the anudātta mark falls on the anubandha ṛ, not on the root vowel, so it marks ātmanepada and does not trigger 7.2.10 (aniṭ). The root is also not in the list of aniṭ exceptions, so it is seṭ and takes the augment इट्. That gives होड् + इ + त = होडित. This rests on my own reading of the accent convention, not a checked source.

<answer>होडित</answer>

This is a derivation from memory of the Dhatupatha and of Panini 1.2.1, not checked against a source.

The root लुट् (luṭ, "to cling, embrace") is added to ण्वुल्, which becomes अक (ण्वुल् → वु → अक). Normally the ṇit suffix would trigger guṇa of the penultimate इक् vowel, as in लेखक from लिख्. Here I take लुटँ to belong to the kuṭādi group of roots, as I recall the list. By Panini 1.2.1 (गाङ्कुटादिभ्योऽञ्णिन्ङित्), a ñit or ṇit suffix after a kuṭādi root counts as ṅit, so guṇa is blocked. The result is लुट् + अक = लुटक.

<answer>लुटक</answer>

I could not confirm this root's class and meaning against the Dhatupatha, so I followed the citation as given.

1. The marker ँ in कितँ makes the root इदित्, so नुम् is inserted: कित् → किन्त्.
2. The root is सेट्, so the suffix takes इट्: किन्त् + इ + तव्य.
3. The इ of किन्त् is followed by a conjunct and is therefore heavy. Guna does not apply (no पुगन्तलघूपध).

The result is किन्तितव्य.

<answer>किन्तितव्य</answer>

I formed this from तक्ष् (takṣ) with the suffix तव्य. I took the root as सेट् (takes the इट् augment), so the form is तक्षितव्य. This rests on my recollection that the Siddhānta-kaumudī gives the future as तक्षिता. I could not confirm it, and if the root were अनिट् the form would instead be तष्टव्य.

<answer>तक्षितव्य</answer>

Following the citation as given, कुटँ is taken as a class 10 root, so the णिच् suffix is added to it before the infinitive suffix.

1. The ँ is the anunāsika marker on the vowel अ, not the इ of an इदित् root, so the नुम् augment does not apply. I am reading the marker this way from memory rather than confirming it against the Dhatupatha text.
2. Before णिच्, the short penultimate उ takes guna by पुगन्तलघूपधस्य (7.3.86). This gives कोट्, so the stem is कोटि- and the form is कोटयति.
3. The तुमुँन् suffix becomes तुम्, with the connecting इ inserted as in other णिच् stems. This gives कोटयितुम्.

<answer>कोटयितुम्</answer>

I derived this by rule rather than from an attested form, and I'm not certain of it.

The root is पुथ्, from the class 4 entry पुथँ हिंसायाम्. I read the anunasika as marking an anudātta root vowel. On that reading the root is single-syllabled and anudātta, so rule 7.2.10 makes it aniṭ, with no इ inserted before the suffix. The suffix क्त reduces to त. Joining पुथ् with त, no sandhi rule alters the थ्, since झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः needs a preceding झष् and थ् is not one. This gives पुथ्त.

If the anunasika were not a reliable aniṭ marker, the seṭ form पुथित would be the alternative.

<answer>पुथ्त</answer>

The root is त्रुट् (class 10, "to cut"). As a Curadi verb it takes the causative-type suffix णिच्, and the penultimate उ takes guṇa, giving त्रोटि. The suffix ल्युँट् then replaces ल्यु with अन, so त्रोटि + अन gives त्रोटन after the णिच् elides.

<answer>त्रोटन</answer>

I derived this by hand and did not check it against a reference.

The root is दॄ (class 9, "to tear open"). With क्त्वा, 7.2.38 (वृतो वा) makes the इट् optional, so दीर्त्वा, दरित्वा and दरीत्वा are all valid. I chose the form without इट्. There क्त्वा behaves as कित्, so 7.1.100 (ऋत इद्धातोः) turns the final ॠ into ईर्.

<answer>दीर्त्वा</answer>

Applying the usual rules, the root षस्तिँ becomes सस्त्. The initial ष् changes to स् (धात्वादेः षः सः), and the final इँ is only an anubandha marker. Because the root is इदित्, it takes the augment नुम्, giving सन्स्त्, and the न् becomes anusvara, giving संस्त्. This analysis of the root and its anubandhas rests on my recollection of the Dhatupatha entry, not a checked source.

The class 2 root takes no विकरण, since शप् is elided (luk). Adding the शतृँ suffix (the participle ending -अत्) gives the stem संस्तत्.

<answer>संस्तत्</answer>

I could not match this root to a known Dhatupatha entry with certainty, so this form rests on an assumption about the root. I read the root as सृम्भ् (षृन्भुँ), with initial ष् becoming स् and the final उँ as an anubandha. I treated it as anit before क्त, like स्रम्भ्, whose participle is स्रब्ध.

On that reading, the nasal is dropped before the kit suffix (अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति). Then भ् + त becomes ब्ध, giving सृब्ध.

<answer>सृब्ध</answer>

The root is जभ् (from जभीँ), with the anubandha ई. Because the root is इदित्, the rule इदितो नुम् धातोः inserts a nasal, giving जम्भ्. The anudātta ई also marks the root as सेट्, so the suffix क्त (which becomes त) takes the augment इट्. The nasal is not dropped, because the deletion rule अनिदितां हल उपधाया क्ङिति applies only to roots that are not इदित्. The result is जम्भ् + इ + त = जम्भित.

<answer>जम्भित</answer>

This is the Curadi root गृ "to know" (विज्ञाने), which takes the causative-type suffix णिच्. The final ऋ takes vṛddhi before णित्, giving गार् + इ = गारि.

Before क्तवतु, the इट् augment is added, so the णिच् is not elided. This gives गारि + इ + तवत्, which contracts to गारितवत्. The uninflected stem is therefore गारितवत्.

<answer>गारितवत्</answer>

I formed this from the root तृन्ह् (class 6, "to injure") with the absolutive suffix क्त्वा. The ऊ marker makes the root optionally seṭ, so I chose the version with the connecting इ.

With इ inserted, क्त्वा is not treated as कित् (1.2.18), so the nasal in the root stays. This gives तृन्ह् + इत्वा, written तृंहित्वा. I did not check this against a Dhatupatha or Kashika text. The alternative without इ would be तॄढ्वा.

<answer>तृंहित्वा</answer>

This is a derivation from the root श्लिष् (भ्वादि, "दाहे") with the suffix तव्य.

1. The उ in श्लिषुँ is an anubandha marker. It makes the root उदित्, so a valādi ārdhadhātuka suffix such as तव्य takes the augment इट् optionally (7.2.44).
2. तव्य is not कित् or ङित्, so the root vowel takes guṇa: श्लिष् → श्लेष्.
3. Without इट्, ष् + त becomes ष्ट by ṣṭutva, giving श्लेष्टव्य. The other valid form, with इट्, is श्लेषितव्य. I chose the form without इट्.

<answer>श्लेष्टव्य</answer>

The root is पुस्त (class 10, meaning "to respect or disrespect"). The steps are:

1. Adding the causative-type suffix णिच् that class 10 roots take gives पुस्ति. There is no guṇa, because the penultimate sound is स्, not a vowel.
2. Adding शप् gives the stem पुस्तय.
3. Adding the atmanepada present participle suffix शानच् gives the ending -आन.
4. The rule आने मुक् inserts म् before -आन after a stem ending in -a, which gives पुस्तयमान.

<answer>पुस्तयमान</answer>

<answer>मंहितृ</answer>
